dialect grammar
grammar equation.snapshot
extension equation
comment none
start document
artifact-mark = "semio" "mathematical.equation.dsl" "v1"

child = child-field+
child-field = {"child-id" "=" text} | {"artifact-id" "=" text} | {"artifact-kind" "=" text} | {"standard" "=" text} | {"subset" "=" text}
expression = expression-field+
expression-field = {"next-label" "=" INT} | {"nodes" "=" "[" node* "]"}
node = node-field+
node-field = {"label" "=" INT} | {"kind" "=" node-kind} | {"lexeme" "=" text} | {"numer" "=" text} | {"denom" "=" text} | {"name" "=" text} | {"terms" "=" indices} | {"factors" "=" indices} | {"base" "=" INT} | {"exponent" "=" INT}
node-kind = "integer" | "rational" | "symbol" | "add" | "mul" | "pow"
indices = "[" INT* "]"
text = IDENT | TEXT

id = OCTET+
number = OCTET+

# Real grammar for `PlaybookSnapshot::print_dsl`/`parse_dsl`: the derived spec-driven text of
# `PlaybookPackRecord` (📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs), the same record the pack encodes. Fields are
# space-separated `key=value` tokens in any order; `title` is optional. A composed child handle is
# the `ArtifactChild` record printed inline: `child_id=<id> target=<artifactId>!<kind>@<standard>/<subset>`.
# `steps` is the `flow` handle's local working scene as its first-party JSON text (a quoted string).
#
#   semio playbook.playbook.dsl v1
#   schema=playbook.program id=facade-generator version="1" title="Facade Panel Generator" steps="[…]" document=child_id=… target="…" flow=child_id=… target="…"
artifact-mark = "semio playbook.playbook.dsl v1"

field = {"schema" "=" TEXT} | {"id" "=" TEXT} | {"version" "=" TEXT} | {"title" "=" TEXT} | {"document" "=" child-handle} | {"flow" "=" child-handle} | {"steps" "=" TEXT}

# the STUBS-AND-PLACEHOLDERS-COMPLETION ticket's brief: "do NOT invent a grammar" when the Rust
# genuinely has no parser). This REPLACES the stale, cross-plugin copy-pasted "canvas layer"
# template (`add-layer`/`remove-layer`/`move id=... dx=... dy=...`) this file previously carried,

# never `dsl::DslDiff`. Compare the two derive expansions: `expand_dsl_diff`
# (🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🗣️dsl/✨️derive/🦀️.rs:1419-1473) generates a real
# `print_diff`/`parse_diff`/`encode_diff`/`decode_diff` (`DiffCodec`) impl; `expand_artifact_schema`

# (125 lines) has no `impl store::ArtifactDsl`/`OpText`/`DiffText for PlaybookDiff` anywhere.

start inference

# 💡️ The inference text form. `RemodelingInference` is computed from a snapshot, never authored,
# and — like `RemodelingDiff` — carries `ToValue`/`FromValue` only (no `dsl::DslRecord`), so its
# single text rendering is the value bridge: `store::to_dsl_value` then the framework's DslValue
# notation — `{ key=value … }` with bare keys sorted by name. That notation is
# `🗣️dsl/🧬️schema/🦀️.rs`'s PRIVATE `print_dsl_value`, reachable only as the payload of a printed
# record field of `Shape::Value`; there is no standalone `DslValue -> String` entry point. Both derived lanes are pinned below with their real inner shape
# (`RemodelingBounds` / `BTreeMap<String, RemodelingPoseDelta>`); `#[value(rename_all = "camelCase")]`
# gives the camelCase keys.

inference = "{" inference-lane* "}"
inference-lane = bounds-lane | relative-camera-poses-lane
bounds-lane = "bounds" "=" bounds-object
relative-camera-poses-lane = "relativeCameraPoses" "=" pose-map
bounds-object = "{" bounds-field* "}"
bounds-field = "boundingBox" "=" bounding-box | "vertexCount" "=" number | "faceCount" "=" number
bounding-box = "{" box-field* "}"
box-field = "max" "=" triple | "min" "=" triple
triple = "[" number number number "]"
pose-map = "{" pose-entry* "}"
pose-entry = key "=" pose-object
pose-object = "{" pose-field* "}"
pose-field = "rotationAngleRad" "=" number | "translationDelta" "=" triple
number = INT | FLOAT
key = IDENT | TEXT

dialect grammar

extension remodeling
start document

# 📖️ The real `.remodeling` document text: what `store::ArtifactDsl::print_dsl` emits for a
# `RemodelingSnapshot` through the framework record printer (`dsl::print`, JoinMode::Document),
# and what `parse_dsl` reads back. Layout (indent/newlines) is lexer trivia, so this grammar is
# a pure token grammar; keyed fields are order-independent on the parse side, so every record
# body below is an unordered set of its real keys rather than a fixed sequence.
# The leading `remodeling.remodeling` mark is the envelope id the `semio remodeling.remodeling.dsl v1`
# preamble reduces to (`SemioEnvelope::envelope_id`), which is what the framework fixture sweep

artifact-mark = "remodeling.remodeling"
document = artifact-mark snapshot-body
snapshot-body = schema-line id-line snapshot-part*
schema-line = "schema" "=" "remodeling.scene"
id-line = "id" "=" name
snapshot-part = assets-map | durable-artifacts-map | calibration-block | params-block | results-block | streams-table | gcps-table

name = IDENT | TEXT
num = INT | FLOAT
quantity = num IDENT
coord3 = "@" num "," num "," num
pair = num "," num
quad = num "," num "," num "," num
quint = num "," num "," num "," num "," num
text-list = "[" name* "]"
cell = PLACEHOLDER

assets-map = "assets" "=" "{" asset-entry* "}"
asset-entry = name "=" child-handle
child-handle = "child_id" "=" name "target" "=" TEXT
durable-artifacts-map = "durable-artifacts" "=" "{" durable-entry* "}"

calibration-block = "calibration" "{" cameras-table rig-table "}"

cameras-header = "[" "id" ":" "TEXT" "label" ":" "TEXT" "model" ":" "TEXT" "fx" ":" "NUM" "fy" ":" "NUM" "cx" ":" "NUM" "cy" ":" "NUM" "skew" ":" "NUM" "distortion" ":" "TUPLE" "rms-reprojection-px" ":" "NUM" "locked" ":" "BOOL" "]"

dialect grammar
grammar remodeling.diff
extension remodeling
start diff

# 🔺️ The sparse-delta text form. `RemodelingDiff` carries `ToValue`/`FromValue` only — it has NO
# `dsl::DslRecord`/`dsl::DslDiff` derive, so it owns no `RecordSpec` and no dedicated printer; its
# only text rendering is the value bridge: `store::to_dsl_value` then the framework's DslValue
# notation, which emits an object as `{ key=value … }` with bare (unquoted) keys sorted by name and
# every lane present as an explicit `null` when unset. That notation is `🗣️dsl/🧬️schema/🦀️.rs`'s
# `print_dsl_value`, which is PRIVATE and reachable only as the payload of a printed record field of
# `Shape::Value` — the framework exposes no standalone `DslValue -> String` entry point today, so a
# test must print a one-field `Shape::Value` record and drop the leading `value=` key token. This grammar therefore pins the 10 real lane keys (camelCase, per
# `#[value(rename_all = "camelCase")]`) at the top level and models each lane payload as the
# generic value notation the bridge emits, rather than inventing a hand-written syntax the code
# does not print. See 📓️w10-grammars.md for the follow-up that would make this a real `DslDiff`.

diff = "{" lane* "}"
lane = artifact-lane | schema-lane | id-lane | streams-lane | assets-lane | durable-artifacts-lane | calibration-lane | params-lane | gcps-lane | results-lane

artifact-lane = "artifact" "=" value
schema-lane = "schema" "=" value
id-lane = "id" "=" value
streams-lane = "streams" "=" value
assets-lane = "assets" "=" value
durable-artifacts-lane = "durableArtifacts" "=" value
calibration-lane = "calibration" "=" value
params-lane = "params" "=" value
gcps-lane = "gcps" "=" value
results-lane = "results" "=" value

value = "null" | "true" | "false" | number | TEXT | array | object
number = INT | FLOAT
array = "[" value* "]"
object = "{" member* "}"
member = key "=" value
key = IDENT | TEXT

# Real grammar for `DrawingSnapshot` — a genuine `#[derive(dsl::DslRecord)]` record
# (🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs:10-32, `#[dsl(id = "drawing.drawing", layout = "lines")]`),
# parsed/printed through the shared `dsl::parse`/`dsl::print` engine (🚪️io/📝️text/📸️snapshot/
# 🦀️.rs:19-37) — NOT the stale add-layer/set-stroke/move-layer/set-fill "canvas layer"
# template this file previously carried. Confirmed field-for-field against the real committed
# fixture `📚️examples/🎬️demo/🖼️assets/🗣️.dsl.semio` (the `semio` emblem, 99 lines):
# scalar fields (`schema=`/`id=`/`title=`) glue onto ONE line; every `#[dsl(key=...)]`-less field
# key is the struct's own field name KEBAB-CASED (`blend-mode=`/`scale-x=`/`scale-y=`/
# `shape-kind=`/`image-key=`/`source-key=`/`simplify-epsilon=`, NOT camelCase — corrected from an
# earlier drafting mistake in this same rewrite); `#[dsl(angle="rad")]` on `rotation` appends a
# bare unit suffix (`rotation=0rad`); a `[f64;N]` fixed-size array (`point`/`color`) prints as a
# bare comma-joined tuple with NO enclosing brackets (`M 1.25,196.933`, `color=0.98,0.584,0,1`);
# a bare identifier string (`is_bare_ident`) prints unquoted (`id=emblem-group`), only a string
# needing escaping is quoted (`name="Semio Emblem"`); `attributes.fill` always prints its own
# `fill { ... }` block (possibly empty) even when no variant is set, while `attributes.stroke` is
# omitted entirely when absent (both fixture-observed, asymmetric despite similar `#[dsl(...)]`
# attrs) — this asymmetry is stated as observed fact, not re-derived from the derive macro source.
document = "schema=" text SP "id=" text opt-title NL layers-block opt-assets opt-artboard

opt-title = (SP "title=" text)?
opt-assets = ("assets" "=" "{" NL asset-entry* "}" NL)?
opt-artboard = ("artboard" "{" NL "width=" number SP "height=" number NL "}" NL)?
# `assets: BTreeMap<String, DrawingImageAsset>` — each entry is `key=` glued directly onto the
# child record's OWN inline field list, no additional wrapping braces (fixture:
# `emblem-trace-source=mime=image/png data="<base64>"`).
asset-entry = IDENT "=" "mime=" text SP "data=" text opt-asset-width opt-asset-height
opt-asset-width = (SP "width=" number)?
opt-asset-height = (SP "height=" number)?

# `layers` is `#[dsl(statements, block)]` — a bare `layers { ... }` block whose items each carry
# their own leading layer-kind keyword (🦀️.rs:281-298, `DrawingLayerNode`'s 7 variants).
layers-block = "layers" "{" layer* "}"
layer = shape-layer / path-layer / text-layer / image-layer / group-layer / boolean-layer / trace-layer

shape-layer = "shape" layer-base "shape-kind=" text opt-rect opt-ellipse opt-circle opt-line opt-polygon
path-layer = "path" layer-base "segments" "{" path-segment* "}"
text-layer = "text" layer-base "x=" number SP "y=" number SP "content=" text SP "size=" number
image-layer = "image" layer-base "image-key=" text SP "width=" number SP "height=" number
group-layer = "group" layer-base "children" "{" layer* "}"
boolean-layer = "boolean" layer-base "operation=" text SP "children=" string-list
trace-layer = "trace" layer-base "source-key=" text trace-params-block
trace-params-block = "params" "{" "threshold=" number SP "simplify-epsilon=" number "}"

# `base: DrawingLayerBase` (`#[serde(flatten)] #[dsl(block)]`, 🦀️.rs:126-138) — a nested
# `base { ... }` block replaces `#[serde(flatten)]` (the dsl engine has no flatten-splice
# primitive yet).
layer-base = "base" "{" "id=" text SP "name=" text SP "visible=" bool SP "locked=" bool SP "opacity=" number SP "blend-mode=" text
     transform-block
     opt-attributes "}"
transform-block = "transform" "{" "x=" number SP "y=" number SP "scale-x=" number SP "scale-y=" number SP "shear=" number SP "rotation=" number "rad" "}"
opt-attributes = ("attributes" "{" "fill-rule=" fill-rule fill-block opt-stroke "}")?
fill-rule = "evenodd" / "nonzero"
fill-block = "fill" "{" fill? "}"
opt-stroke = ("stroke" "{" "color=" number4 SP "width=" number SP "cap=" stroke-cap SP "join=" stroke-join opt-dash "}")?
stroke-cap = "butt" / "round" / "square"
stroke-join = "miter" / "round" / "bevel"
opt-dash = (SP "dash=" number-list)?

# `fill: Option<FillStyle>` (`#[dsl(statements, block)]`) — own leading keyword per variant
# (🦀️.rs:58-79). `stops` is `#[dsl(table)]` — a compact SoA `[col:TYPE ...] {rows}` table,
# not modeled column-for-column below (inferred, not fixture-verified — the emblem fixture never
# uses a gradient fill).
fill = solid-fill / linear-gradient-fill / radial-gradient-fill
solid-fill = "solid" "{" "color=" number4 "}"
linear-gradient-fill = "linearGradient" "{" "x1=" number SP "y1=" number SP "x2=" number SP "y2=" number SP "stops" stops-table "}"
radial-gradient-fill = "radialGradient" "{" "cx=" number SP "cy=" number SP "r=" number SP "stops" stops-table "}"
stops-table = "[" "offset:NUM" SP "color:NUM4" "]" "{" stop-row* "}"
stop-row = number SP number4

opt-rect = ("rect" "{" "x=" number SP "y=" number SP "width=" number SP "height=" number "}")?
opt-ellipse = ("ellipse" "{" "cx=" number SP "cy=" number SP "rx=" number SP "ry=" number "}")?
opt-circle = ("circle" "{" "cx=" number SP "cy=" number SP "r=" number "}")?
opt-line = ("line" "{" "x1=" number SP "y1=" number SP "x2=" number SP "y2=" number "}")?
opt-polygon = ("polygon" "{" "points=" point-list "}")?

# `PathSegment` — a genuine SVG-path-data subset, one uppercase command letter per keyword, every
# field `#[dsl(positional)]` (🦀️.rs:306-355): `M x,y`/`L x,y`/`Q cx,cy x,y`/
# `C c1x,c1y c2x,c2y x,y`/`A rx ry rotation large-arc sweep x,y`/`Z` — fixture-confirmed:
# `M 1.25,196.933`, `L 36.25,161.125`, `Z`.
path-segment = move-segment / line-segment / quad-segment / cubic-segment / arc-segment / close-segment
move-segment = "M" SP point
line-segment = "L" SP point
quad-segment = "Q" SP point SP point
cubic-segment = "C" SP point SP point SP point
arc-segment = "A" SP number SP number SP number SP bool SP bool SP point
close-segment = "Z"

# `[f64;2]`/`[f64;4]` fixed-size arrays print as a bare comma-joined tuple, NO brackets
# (fixture: `M 1.25,196.933`, `color=0.98,0.584,0,1`) — corrected from an earlier drafting
# mistake in this same rewrite that had bracketed them like a `Vec`.
point = number "," number
number4 = number "," number "," number "," number
# `Vec<[f64;2]>`/`Vec<f64>`/`Vec<String>` (`points=`/`dash=`/`children=` on a boolean layer) are
# inferred to print bracket-wrapped, matching every other `Vec<T>` list shape in this ticket's
# other grammars — NOT independently fixture-verified (the emblem fixture has no polygon layer,
# no dashed stroke, and no boolean layer).
point-list = "[" point* "]"
number-list = "[" number* "]"
string-list = "[" text* "]"

# A string prints BARE when it lexes back as one `is_bare_ident` token (fixture: `id=emblem-group`,
# `mime=image/png`), quoted+escaped otherwise (fixture: `name="Semio Emblem"`).
text = bare-text / quoted-text
bare-text = OCTET+
quoted-text = DQUOTE OCTET* DQUOTE
number = INT / FLOAT
bool = "true" / "false"

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.svg.snapshot
extension svg
start document
comment none

# Real one-line `ArtifactDsl::print_dsl`/`parse_dsl` shape this artifact ALREADY emits: the semio
# preamble followed by `🔨️modules/🧬️mutation-support/🦀️.rs`'s `encode_snapshot`/`decode_snapshot`
# body -- the SAME structured, hex-payload frame the sibling `../../🔺️diff/📝️text` and
# `../../🧬️mutations/📝️text` grammars describe, whose shared primitives (`opt-*`, `xml-node`,
# `external-id`, …) are restated here verbatim so this leaf grammar stays self-contained (a
# cross-facet `use` doesn't resolve at recognize time yet, `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §2.1).
#
# This REPLACES the earlier raw-`.svg`-markup grammar. That one described `write_svg_xml`'s output,
# which is what `export_utf8` (the document's own native wire) emits and what `parse_dsl`'s
# ENVELOPE-LESS branch imports — never what `print_dsl` writes under the preamble. The two branches
# are the whole point of `parse_dsl`'s own two-branch contract (`../../📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs`), and
# `grammar_conformance_law` recognizes the PREAMBLE branch, so this file has to describe that one.
#
# `comment none`: hex payloads are lowercase-only and never contain `#`, and no `#`-to-EOL comment
# may swallow a line of one; same directive the diff/mutations grammars carry.
#
# `hex` (bare `hex`, referenced below but deliberately NOT defined as a production here) is the
# framework's built-in `hex` MACRO -- see the mandatory-macro rationale in `📖️grammar-recipe.md`
# §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall 2 (a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*` production never backtracks and would silently
# swallow a following bareword literal).
artifact-mark = "stdio.svg"
document = artifact-mark snapshot-body

# `encode_snapshot`: `[hex(schema),opt-node(root),opt-doctype,opt-declaration,[prolog-nodes],[epilog-nodes]]`.
snapshot-body = "[" hex "," opt-xml-node "," opt-doctype "," opt-declaration "," "[" node-item* "]" "," "[" node-item* "]" "]"

# `encode_option`'s uniform tri-state shape (`📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.4): `[0]` (None) /
# `[1,<value>]` (Some).
opt-hex = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," hex "]"
opt-bool = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," bool-lit "]"
bool-lit = "0" | "1"
opt-xml-node = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," xml-node "]"

# `enc_declaration`/`dec_declaration`:
# `[hex(version),opt-hex(encoding),opt-bool(standalone),bool-lit(quote)]` -- the trailing flag is
# `XmlQuote` (`0` = the `"` spelling, `1` = `'`), real document state per XML 1.0 §2.8, not
# retained source text (`enc_quote`/`dec_quote`).
opt-declaration = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," declaration-lit "]"
declaration-lit = "[" hex "," opt-hex "," opt-bool "," bool-lit "]"

# `enc_doctype`/`dec_doctype`: `[prolog-position,hex(name),opt-external-id,[dtd-declarations]]`.
opt-doctype = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," doctype-lit "]"
doctype-lit = "[" INT "," hex "," opt-external-id "," "[" dtd-declaration-list? "]" "]"
opt-external-id = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," external-id "]"
external-id = "S" "[" hex "]" | "P" "[" hex "," hex "]"
dtd-declaration-list = dtd-declaration dtd-declaration-tail*
dtd-declaration-tail = "," dtd-declaration
dtd-declaration = "E" "[" bool-lit "," hex "," hex "]"

# `enc_xml_node`/`dec_xml_node` -- `E`=Element, `T`=Text, `D`=CDATA, `M`=Comment,
# `P`=ProcessingInstruction. Genuinely recursive: an element's children slot references
# `node-item` which references `xml-node` back -- the same self-recursion `📖️grammar-recipe.md`
# §1.3(g) documents as already-proven-safe.
xml-node = "E" "[" hex "," "[" attr-item* "]" "," "[" node-item* "]" "]" | "T" "[" hex "]" | "D" "[" hex "]" | "M" "[" hex "]" | "P" "[" hex "," hex "]"
attr-item = "[" hex "," hex "]" ","?
node-item = xml-node ","?

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SVG-specific attribute-VALUE micro-grammars (per this wave's brief) -- documentary productions,
# deliberately UNREACHABLE from `start=document`. `attr-item = "[" hex "," hex "]"` above already
# captures a whole attribute value as ONE opaque `hex` payload -- there is no dialect-level
# mechanism to re-tokenize an already-consumed token's contents against a DIFFERENT,
# attribute-NAME-conditioned production (no "if the previous attribute's name was X, switch
# grammars for its value" primitive exists), so nothing below can ever be wired into the
# `document` production tree above. They exist purely to document, as precisely as the token
# dialect allows, the REAL internal structure this artifact's own Rust codec
# (`../../🦀️.rs`'s `NumCursor`/`parse_view_box`/`parse_points`/`parse_transform_list`/
# `parse_path_data`) imposes once an attribute value string has been extracted -- matching the
# W0 census's own conclusion for this row ("inner mini-languages ... stay hand-written
# regardless") while still modeling everything that genuinely IS structural, per the brief.
#
# `viewBox="min-x min-y width height"` (`parse_view_box`) -- 4 comma-or-space-separated numbers
# (SVG's own `<comma-wsp>` grammar -- `NumCursor::skip_wsp_comma` treats a literal `,` and
# whitespace interchangeably as a separator, so the comma below is optional either way).
view-box-value = number ","? number ","? number ","? number
number = INT | FLOAT

# `points="x1,y1 x2,y2 ..."` (`parse_points`, polyline/polygon) -- an even-length run of
# comma/space-separated number pairs.
points-value = point {","? point}*
point = number ","? number

# `transform="translate(10,20) scale(2) rotate(90,5,5) ..."` (`parse_transform_list`) -- a
# space-separated list of `name(args)` function calls; `(`/`)` are already real single-char lexer
# tokens (distinct from this dialect's own `{ }` GROUPING metasyntax, `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §3
# pitfall 1), so this is real structure, not a fabricated approximation.
transform-value = transform-fn*
transform-fn = IDENT "(" number-list ")"
number-list = {number ","?}*

# `d="M10,10 L20,20 Z"` (`parse_path_data`) -- MODELED ONLY for the case where every command has
# its own EXPLICIT leading letter, matching `parse_path_data`'s own per-letter match arms and each
# command's fixed, letter-determined argument arity (SVG 1.1 spec §8.3.2). Two real behaviors of
# the Rust parser are genuinely NOT representable at this token-based layer -- filed as
# `mechanism_gaps` id `svg-path-data-implicit-and-flag-squeeze` (`engine_area`: grammar dialect /
# lexer): (1) IMPLICIT command repetition (a number run with no leading letter reuses the
# PREVIOUS command's letter -- a STATEFUL, not context-free, dispatch no production-based grammar
# can express); (2) the arc command's flag-digit SQUEEZE (`"A5 5 0 108 8"`'s `108` must decompose
# into flags `1`,`0` then the number `8`, per `NumCursor::parse_flag`'s own doc comment) -- but
# `108` has ALREADY been consumed as one atomic `INT` token by the shared lexer's tokenization
# pass, before any grammar-level production ever runs; no amount of grammar authoring can
# retroactively un-lex a token. Both gaps are pre-existing lexer/dialect limits, not bugs in this
# artifact's own Rust parser (which handles both correctly, per `path_arc_flag_squeeze_decomposes_correctly`
# in `../../🦀️.rs`'s own test module).
d-value = path-command+
path-command = "M" number number | "L" number number | "H" number | "V" number | "C" number number number number number number | "S" number number number number | "Q" number number number number | "T" number number | "A" number number number flag flag number number | "Z"
flag = "0" | "1"

# `style="fill: red; stroke: blue"` (`parse_style_decls`) -- an honest opaque leaf, NOT modeled:
# the real Rust codec is a naive `;`-split/first-`:`-split KEY/VALUE pair extractor whose VALUE
# side (`red`, `#ff0000`, `2px`, `url(#g1)`, ...) is a plain, never-further-typed `String` -- there
# is no fixed grammar to restate here without fabricating structure the codec itself doesn't
# impose (`style`'s whole attribute value stays the opaque `hex` payload `attr-item` already
# captures above).

# `../../🦀️.rs` (`print_svg_diff`/`parse_svg_diff`), replacing the F6-era placeholder that

# shape field-for-field (`declaration`/`doctype`/`root`, same `Element`/`Text`/`Replace`
# `SvgNodeDiff` tree) -- per Phase 1's explicit design decision svg declares its OWN diff types even
# though it reuses xml's node model (`../🦀️.rs`'s own doc comment) -- so this grammar

# `comment none`: kept for consistency with the sibling ../../📸️snapshot/📝️text grammar; not
# strictly required by any token this grammar's own alphabet produces (hex payloads are
# lowercase-only, never containing `#`).
#
# `hex` (bare `hex`, referenced below but deliberately NOT defined as a production in this file) is
# the framework's built-in `hex` MACRO -- see the mandatory-macro rationale in
# `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall 2 (a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*` production never

opt-bool = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," bool-lit "]"
bool-lit = "0" | "1"

# `enc_declaration`/`dec_declaration`:
# `[hex(version),opt-hex(encoding),opt-bool(standalone),bool-lit(quote)]` -- the trailing flag is
# `XmlQuote` (`0` = the `"` spelling, `1` = `'`), real document state per XML 1.0 §2.8, not
# retained source text (`enc_quote`/`dec_quote`).
opt-declaration = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," declaration-lit "]"
declaration-lit = "[" hex "," opt-hex "," opt-bool "," bool-lit "]"
opt-doctype = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," doctype-lit "]"
doctype-lit = "[" INT "," hex "," opt-external-id "," "[" dtd-declaration-list? "]" "]"
opt-external-id = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," external-id "]"
external-id = "S" "[" hex "]" | "P" "[" hex "," hex "]"
dtd-declaration-list = dtd-declaration dtd-declaration-tail*
dtd-declaration-tail = "," dtd-declaration
dtd-declaration = "E" "[" bool-lit "," hex "," hex "]"

node-diff = "E" "[" opt-hex "," opt-attrs-diff "," opt-children-diff "]" | "T" "[" opt-hex "]" | "R" "[" opt-xml-node "]"
opt-attrs-diff = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," attrs-diff-body "]"
opt-children-diff = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," children-diff-body "]"
opt-xml-node = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," xml-node "]"
prolog-tok = "prolog" "=" node-list
epilog-tok = "epilog" "=" node-list

# `enc_attrs_diff`/`dec_attrs_diff` -- `[removed];[modified];[added]`, name-keyed

attr-modified-item = hex ":" hex ","?
attr-added-item = INT ":" hex ":" hex ","?

# `enc_children_diff`/`dec_children_diff` -- `[removed];[modified];[added]`, index-keyed.
children-diff-body = "[" child-removed-item* "]" ";" "[" child-modified-item* "]" ";" "[" child-added-item* "]"
child-removed-item = INT ","?
child-modified-item = INT ":" node-diff ","?
child-added-item = INT ":" xml-node ","?

# `enc_xml_node`/`dec_xml_node` -- restated here (svg reuses xml's `XmlNode` type directly, per
# Phase 1's own design, cited in this file's own header comment) so this leaf grammar is
# self-contained, matching the repo's existing per-facet convention.
xml-node = "E" "[" hex "," "[" attr-item* "]" "," "[" node-item* "]" "]" | "T" "[" hex "]" | "D" "[" hex "]" | "M" "[" hex "]" | "P" "[" hex "," hex "]"
attr-item = "[" hex "," hex "]" ","?
node-item = xml-node ","?

# outside this dialect's alphabet entirely). `print_dsl` is `wrap_text(envelope, body)` where `body`
# is `self.bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()` -- a CONTINUOUS run of lowercase hex
# digit pairs, no separators, no whitespace (confirmed by direct read, not assumed). The framework's
# own `m5`/artifact-level conformance harness (`dsl_body_from_fixture`,
# `🗣️dsl/🧪️fixture/🦀️-sweep.rs`) strips the mandatory `semio stdio.binary.dsl v1` preamble

# `Recognizer::recognize` -- so `document` starts with that literal, not the full preamble line
# (matching json/csv's own pilot precedent exactly). No `ws`/`NL` production is needed: whitespace,
# newlines, and comments are lexer trivia, stripped by `Recognizer::recognize` before matching
# begins (confirmed by reading that function).

# P2-P1-fix note (mandatory reading, `p2-p1-fix-report.md`): an open-ended hex run MUST be the
# framework's built-in `hex` MACRO (bare `hex`, no matching production here -- `Symbol::Ref` falls
# back production-then-macro automatically), never a hand-rolled `{INT | IDENT}*`-shaped production
# -- `Symbol::Star` is a single greedy, non-backtracking pass, and the macro's own
# `match_macro_span` tries the largest span first and backtracks correctly (plus already supports
# the empty-body case, `BinarySnapshot::default()`'s `bytes: vec![]`). `hex-body` here has nothing
# following it to backtrack off of (it is the last token in the document), so this also sidesteps
# every hex/keyword-adjacency pitfall that macro was built for in the first place.

# RFC 4180 §2: quote-state-aware record/field grammar, matching this artifact's real
# `parse_csv_records` tokenizer (⚙️engine/component.rs:20-69) exactly — not a "hex dump"
# shortcut, not the pre-Phase-2 ABNF placeholder this file used to contain.
comment none
string double doubled

# `dsl::fixture_sweep::m5_handcrafted_grammar_conformance::dsl_body_from_fixture` feeds the
# Recognizer "<envelope-id>\n<body>" (SemioEnvelope::envelope_id = "plugin.artifact", the real
# preamble line's trailing "v<n>" already stripped by the harness) — the shared lexer treats
# both the preamble's own newline AND every record-terminating CR/LF as trivia (never surfaced
# as tokens to this grammar, see this artifact's report, mechanism_gaps "csv-newline-trivia"),
# so `envelope-mark` and the first record sit directly adjacent in the significant token stream.
envelope-mark = "stdio.csv"
document = envelope-mark document-body

# RFC 4180 §2 rule 1/2: one-or-more records. This dialect has no NEWLINE terminal (see
# mechanism_gaps above) — a record boundary is recovered structurally instead: `record` greedily
# consumes every comma-adjacent field in the significant token stream, which is exactly one
# physical line's worth, because a real source CR/LF always breaks the shared lexer's token
# scan even though the resulting Newline token is then dropped as trivia before this grammar
# ever sees it (proven for this artifact's own real fixture, see the conformance test).
document-body = record+
record = field {"," field}*
field = quoted-field | unquoted-field

# RFC 4180 §2 rule 5: a quoted field may itself legally contain the field/record delimiters
# (comma, CR, LF) as literal data, with a literal `"` escaped by doubling (`""`). The
# `string double doubled` mode declared above makes the shared lexer decode exactly this —
# one TEXT token per quoted field, with every embedded comma/CR/LF/doubled-quote already
# resolved, never surfacing as separate COMMA/record-boundary tokens. This is the real fix for
# the "structural-comma-vs-quoted-comma" gap the P2-W0 recon census flagged for this artifact.
# Known real limitation (see this artifact's report, mechanism_gaps
# "csv-quoted-field-embedded-newline"): the shared lexer's `Doubled` string scanner treats a raw
# `\n` mid-string as unterminated even in forgiving mode (🔍️lexer/component.rs:393-398), so a
# quoted field containing a LITERAL embedded newline (also legal per RFC 4180 §2 rule 5) is not
# tokenized as one TEXT token — this artifact's own fixture deliberately avoids that input shape.
quoted-field = TEXT

# RFC 4180 §2 rule 6: an unquoted field is a run of TEXTDATA (any octet except comma, CR, LF,
# DQUOTE — %x20-21 / %x23-2B / %x2D-7E / %x80-10FFFF). This dialect's fixed token alphabet can
# only directly represent the IDENT/INT/FLOAT-shaped subset of TEXTDATA (see this artifact's
# report, mechanism_gaps "csv-unquoted-textdata-alphabet") — an unquoted field is zero-or-more
# such atoms; inter-atom whitespace is lexer trivia here, same treatment json's grammar already
# gives its own escape-decoding boundary (P2-W0 §1a).
unquoted-field = field-atom*
field-atom = IDENT | INT | FLOAT

#
# `hex` (bare `hex`, deliberately NOT defined as a production here) is the framework's built-in `hex`
# MACRO (`📖️grammar/🦀️.rs`'s `default_macros`/`macro_hex_ok`) — a run of lowercase hex
# digits, incl. the empty string. This dialect has no dedicated hex-digit-run TERMINAL, so a hex
# string fragments unpredictably across the fixed INT/IDENT/FLOAT token boundaries depending on its
# own digit/letter mix (see this artifact's report, mechanism_gaps "csv-hex-token-fragmentation");
# `hex` MUST be the macro, not a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*`-shaped production, for two independent,
# live-confirmed reasons: (1) a production's `Star` never backtracks (`Symbol::Star`'s doc comment),
# so `set-field-op`'s real wire shape `value=<hex> quoted=<bit>` — the literal `quoted` tokenizes as
# a plain `IDENT`, exactly like a stray hex letter run would — gets silently swallowed INTO a greedy
# `hex` Star, desyncing everything after it; (2) a hex run containing `<digits>e<digits>` (`e` is
# itself a valid lowercase hex digit) lexes as one `FLOAT` token, not alternating `INT`/`IDENT`. The
# macro's own backtracking (`Recognizer::match_macro_span` tries the largest token span first and
# shrinks until `try_match` accepts) handles both, with no grammar-file workaround needed — same
# mechanism as the sibling json artifact's
# `../../../../../🧾️json/…/🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio`'s `hex` doc comment.

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.step.inference
extension step.inference
start document

document = header body
header = "schema" SP "s.stdio.step.inference" NL
body = payload NL?
payload = OCTET+

# 📖️ Real ISO 10303-21 Part-21 exchange-file grammar (P2-FG1), matching this facet's own
# `engine::part21::{Lexer, parse_part21, write_part21}` tokenizer 1:1
# (`⚙️engine/📐️part21/🦀️.rs`) — replaces the old one-line-header ABNF placeholder this
# file used to contain. STEP's `#N=...` entity-ref sigil collides with the shared lexer's DEFAULT
# `#`-to-EOL comment convention, so `comment line none` + `comment block "/*" "*/"` (Part-21's real
# comment form) resolve that collision per M1's own documented STEP-shaped worked example.
# `string single doubled` turns on `''`-doubling decode for every `'...'` token (Part-21's own
# string escape convention — the `\X\HH\`/`\X2\HHHH...\X0\` unicode escapes stay opaque CONTENT
# inside that one TEXT token, never separately modeled — `StringEscape::Doubled` only interprets
# `''`, leaving backslash runs untouched, confirmed by direct read of the shared lexer). `print_dsl`
# wraps a `semio stdio.step.dsl v1` preamble line the harness strips to the bare envelope id
# (`"stdio.step"`) before this grammar ever sees the body, matching every pilot's own
# `grammar_conformance_law` reconstruction convention. https://www.iso.org/standard/63141.html
dialect grammar
grammar stdio.step.snapshot
extension step
start document
comment line none
comment block "/*" "*/"
string single doubled

document = envelope-mark exchange-file
envelope-mark = "stdio.step"

# `write_part21`'s exact output shape: `ISO-10303-21;` `HEADER;` the three standard records in
# fixed order, `ENDSEC;` `DATA;` every instance, `ENDSEC;` `END-ISO-10303-21;`.
exchange-file = "ISO-10303-21" ";" "HEADER" ";" file-description-record file-name-record file-schema-record "ENDSEC" ";" "DATA" ";" instance* "ENDSEC" ";" "END-ISO-10303-21" ";"
file-description-record = "FILE_DESCRIPTION" "(" value-list ")" ";"
file-name-record = "FILE_NAME" "(" value-list ")" ";"
file-schema-record = "FILE_SCHEMA" "(" value-list ")" ";"

# One `#N=TYPE(args);` simple instance, or a spec-legal `#N=(TYPE1(...)TYPE2(...));` complex
# instance (`StepEntity::complex`, ISO 10303-21 §4.2) — real, not a hypothetical, rare in AP214,
# common in IFC's select-type disambiguation (the shared `part21` tokenizer both artifacts reuse).
instance = "#" INT "=" instance-body ";"
instance-body = entity-record | "(" entity-record+ ")"
entity-record = IDENT "(" value-list ")"

# `value` per `Part21Value`/`write_value`: `$` unset, `*` derived, `#N` reference, `'...'` string
# (TEXT), `.NAME.` enumeration (DOTENUM), a plain number (real values always carry a trailing dot
# via `format_real` — still `INT | FLOAT` since a negative whole real like `-3.` still lexes as
# FLOAT only once the dot is present; the bare-INT alternative here covers the `Int` variant, which
# never gets a dot), a parenthesized list (recursive aggregate), or a typed/defined-type wrapper
# (`IFCLENGTHMEASURE(3000.)`-shaped — an EXPRESS keyword immediately followed by its own value
# list, indistinguishable at this level from a top-level instance record; disambiguated only by
# nesting position, per `StepValue::TypedValue`'s own doc comment).
value-list = {step-value {"," step-value}*}?
step-value = "$" | "*" | "#" INT | TEXT | DOTENUM | INT | FLOAT | "(" value-list ")" | IDENT "(" value-list ")"

# 📖️ P2-FG1: real `DiffCodec::print_diff`/`parse_diff` shape for `StepDiff`, hand-rolled since
# `#[derive(dsl::DslDiff)]` fails (real `cargo check` output, `StepEntitiesDiff`/`StepValue: DslField`
# unsatisfied — see `🔺️diff/🦀️.rs`'s own doc comment). One line of space-separated
# `name=value` tokens, only the CHANGED top-level fields present, in declared field order — every
# literal copied verbatim from `print_step_diff`'s real body, not invented. Replaces the old
# serde-JSON `{"fileDescription":...}` ABNF placeholder this file used to contain.
dialect grammar
grammar stdio.step.diff
start document

document = file-description-tok? file-name-tok? file-schema-tok? entities-tok?
file-description-tok = "file-description" "=" file-description
file-name-tok = "file-name" "=" file-name
file-schema-tok = "file-schema" "=" file-schema
entities-tok = "entities" "=" entities-diff

# `enc_entities_diff`: `[removed-ids];[modified];[added]` — id-keyed collection triple (§1.4's
# copy-pasteable shape). `modified` items are `id:entity-diff`; `added` items are `index:entity`
# (FINAL-position index, matching this program's own `added` semantics convention).
entities-diff = "[" u64-list "]" ";" "[" entity-modified-list "]" ";" "[" entity-added-list "]"
u64-list = {INT {"," INT}*}?
entity-modified-list = {entity-modified {"," entity-modified}*}?
entity-modified = INT ":" entity-diff
entity-added-list = {entity-added {"," entity-added}*}?
entity-added = INT ":" entity

# `enc_entity_diff`: `[nameOpt,argsOpt,complexOpt]` — every field independently `[0]`/`[1,value]`
# tri-state-tagged (§1.4's Tri-state pattern; `Option<T>`, never a genuine `Option<Option<T>>` here).
entity-diff = "[" name-opt "," args-opt "," complex-opt "]"
name-opt = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," hex "]"
args-opt = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," args-diff "]"
complex-opt = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," "[" complex-list "]" "]"

# `enc_args_diff`: SAME `[removed];[modified];[added]` collection-triple shape, index-keyed (Part-21
# entity argument lists are positional). Items are `StepValue` directly — a weak collection, the
# "diff" IS the whole new value, no further sub-diffing.
args-diff = "[" usize-list "]" ";" "[" arg-modified-list "]" ";" "[" arg-added-list "]"
usize-list = {INT {"," INT}*}?
arg-modified-list = {arg-modified {"," arg-modified}*}?
arg-modified = INT ":" step-value
arg-added-list = {arg-added {"," arg-added}*}?
arg-added = INT ":" step-value

# `StepValue`'s single-uppercase-letter tag scheme — see the sibling mutations grammar's identical
# doc comment for the full rationale (own copy per this dialect's per-file convention).
step-value = "U" "[" "]" | "D" "[" "]" | "I" "[" INT "]" | "R" "[" real-num "]" | "S" "[" hex "]" | "E" "[" hex "]" | "F" "[" INT "]" | "A" "[" value-list "]" | "T" "[" hex "," step-value "]"
real-num = INT | FLOAT
value-list = {step-value {"," step-value}*}?

entity = "[" INT "," hex "," "[" value-list "]" "," "[" complex-list "]" "]"
complex-list = {complex-item {"," complex-item}*}?
complex-item = "[" hex "," "[" value-list "]" "]"

file-description = "[" "[" hex-list "]" "," hex "]"
file-name = "[" hex "," hex "," "[" hex-list "]" "," "[" hex-list "]" "," hex "," hex "," hex "]"
file-schema = "[" hex-list "]"
hex-list = {hex {"," hex}*}?

# 📖️ P2-FG1: real `OpText::print_op`/`parse_op` shape for `StepMutation`, hand-rolled since
# `#[derive(dsl::DslOps)]` fails (real `cargo check` output, `StepEntity`/`StepValue: DslField`
# unsatisfied — see `🧬️mutations/🦀️.rs`'s own doc comment). One `keyword key=value ...`
# line, space-separated, keys in the field's declared struct order. Every literal below is copied
# verbatim from `print_step_mutation`'s real match arms
# (`✏️s/…/📐️step/🏅️standards/🔖️ap214/🪆️subsets/🧱️base/🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🦀️.rs`), not
# invented. Replaces the old serde-JSON `{"mutation":"...",...}` ABNF placeholder this file used to
# contain — that shape was never emitted by the real hand-rolled codec even before this rewrite.
dialect grammar
grammar stdio.step.mutation
start document

document = set-snapshot | set-file-description | set-file-name | set-file-schema | insert-entity | remove-entity | set-entity-name | set-entity-arg | insert-entity-arg | remove-entity-arg

set-snapshot = "set-snapshot" "snapshot" "=" step-snapshot
set-file-description = "set-file-description" "file-description" "=" file-description
set-file-name = "set-file-name" "file-name" "=" file-name
set-file-schema = "set-file-schema" "file-schema" "=" file-schema
insert-entity = "insert-entity" "index" "=" INT "entity" "=" entity
remove-entity = "remove-entity" "id" "=" INT
set-entity-name = "set-entity-name" "id" "=" INT "name" "=" hex
set-entity-arg = "set-entity-arg" "id" "=" INT "arg-index" "=" INT "value" "=" step-value
insert-entity-arg = "insert-entity-arg" "id" "=" INT "arg-index" "=" INT "value" "=" step-value
remove-entity-arg = "remove-entity-arg" "id" "=" INT "arg-index" "=" INT

# `StepValue`'s single-uppercase-letter tag scheme (`enc_value`/`dec_value`): `U[]` Unset, `D[]`
# Derived, `I[n]` Integer, `R[n]` Real (Rust's bare `Display` for `f64` — never forces a decimal
# point, unlike Part-21 text's own `format_real`, so a whole real prints INT-shaped), `S[hex]`
# String, `E[hex]` Enum, `F[n]` reFerence (`R` already taken by Real), `A[items]` Aggregate
# (recursive list), `T[hex,value]` TypedValue (recursive, one wrapped value).
step-value = "U" "[" "]" | "D" "[" "]" | "I" "[" INT "]" | "R" "[" real-num "]" | "S" "[" hex "]" | "E" "[" hex "]" | "F" "[" INT "]" | "A" "[" value-list "]" | "T" "[" hex "," step-value "]"
real-num = INT | FLOAT
value-list = {step-value {"," step-value}*}?

# `enc_entity`: `[id,hexname,[args],[complex]]`. `enc_complex`/`complex-item`: `[hexname,[args]]`.
entity = "[" INT "," hex "," "[" value-list "]" "," "[" complex-list "]" "]"
complex-list = {complex-item {"," complex-item}*}?
complex-item = "[" hex "," "[" value-list "]" "]"
entity-list = {entity {"," entity}*}?
hex-list = {hex {"," hex}*}?

# `enc_file_description`: `[[desc-strings],implementation-level]`.
file-description = "[" "[" hex-list "]" "," hex "]"
# `enc_file_name`: `[name,timestamp,[author],[organization],preprocessor,originating,authorization]`.
file-name = "[" hex "," hex "," "[" hex-list "]" "," "[" hex-list "]" "," hex "," hex "," hex "]"
# `enc_file_schema`: `[schema-strings]`.
file-schema = "[" hex-list "]"

# `enc_step_snapshot` (only reachable via `SetSnapshot`'s payload): `[schema,fileDescription,
# fileName,fileSchema,[entities]]`.
step-snapshot = "[" hex "," file-description "," file-name "," file-schema "," "[" entity-list "]" "]"

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.tsv.inference
extension tsv.inference
start document

document = header body
header = "schema" SP "stdio.tsv.inference" NL
body = payload NL?
payload = OCTET+

dialect grammar stdio.tsv.snapshot
root = file
; envelope preamble line + its trailing newline are stripped before this grammar runs
; (store::semio_format::split_text_preamble). Real IANA text/tab-separated-values grammar:
; https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/text/tab-separated-values
; NO quoting/escaping mechanism exists — a field can never legally contain a literal TAB, CR
; or LF byte; there is no way to escape one (contrast with csv's optional DQUOTE wrapping).
file = [record *(line-ending record)] [line-ending]
record = field *(TAB field)
field = *TEXTDATA
TAB = %x09
line-ending = "\r\n" / "\n"                     ; whichever convention THIS file uses, uniformly
TEXTDATA = %x00-08 / %x0B-0C / %x0E-FF           ; any byte except TAB (0x09), CR (0x0D), LF (0x0A)

dialect grammar stdio.tsv.diff
root = diff
; wire text is the hand-rolled space-separated token grammar `protocol::DiffCodec` prints
; (see 🦀️.rs `print_tsv_diff`/`parse_tsv_diff`) — not JSON. Every top-level field
; that changed appears as one `name=value` token; string/row values are lowercase hex (TSV
; cells legally contain almost anything except tab/CR/LF, which this grammar's own separators
; are built from).
diff = token *(SP token)
token = "trailing-newline=" BIT
      / "line-ending=" ("lf" / "crlf")
      / "records{" removed ";" modified ";" added "}"
removed = "[" *(INT ",") "]"
modified = "[" *(INT ":" rowdiff ",") "]"
added = "[" *(INT ":" row ",") "]"
rowdiff = "[0]" / "[1,[" *(option ",") "]]"
row = "[" *(hexstr ",") "]"
option = "[0]" / "[1," hexstr "]"
hexstr = *HEXDIG
BIT = "0" / "1"
SP = " "

dialect grammar stdio.tsv.mutations
root = mutation
; wire text is the hand-rolled `keyword arg=value ...` token line `protocol::OpText` prints
; (see 🦀️.rs `print_tsv_mutation`/`parse_tsv_mutation`) — not JSON.
mutation = "set-snapshot" SP "snapshot=" hexsnapshot
         / "set-trailing-newline" SP "trailing-newline=" BIT
         / "set-line-ending" SP "line-ending=" ("lf" / "crlf")
         / "insert-row" SP "index=" INT SP "row=" hexrow
         / "remove-row" SP "index=" INT
         / "set-cell" SP "row-index=" INT SP "field-index=" INT SP "value=" hexstr
SP = " "
BIT = "0" / "1"
hexstr = *HEXDIG
hexrow = "[" *(hexstr ",") "]"
hexsnapshot = "[" hexstr "," BIT "," ("lf" / "crlf") ",[" *(hexrow ",") "]]"

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.xlsx.inference

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.xlsx.diff
extension xlsx
start document
comment none
string double backslash

# Real one-line `DiffCodec::print_diff` shape of `../../🦀️.rs` (`🔖️TopLevel` region): the RFC 8259 JSON of
# `XlsxDiff`'s `ToValue` (`dsl::json::to_json_string`) -- one object whose members are the diff's present
# top-level fields (`opc`, `xmlParts`; an absent field is skipped, so the empty diff prints `{}`).
document = "{" "}" | "{" diff-field {"," diff-field}* "}"
diff-field = "opc" ":" object | "xmlParts" ":" object

# ── RFC 8259 value syntax, restated from `🧾️json`'s own snapshot grammar: `string double backslash`
# decodes every `"..."` TEXT token's escapes, whitespace is lexer trivia, `{...}*` is the only grouping. ──
value = object | array | json-string | number | "true" | "false" | "null"
object = "{" "}" | "{" member {"," member}* "}"
member = json-string ":" value
array = "[" "]" | "[" value {"," value}* "]"
json-string = TEXT
number = INT | FLOAT

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.xlsx.mutations
extension xlsx
start document
comment none

# Real one-line `OpText::print_op`/`parse_op` shape of `../../🦀️.rs` (`print_xlsx_mutation`/
# `parse_xlsx_mutation`, `🔖️MutationCodec` region): `keyword arg=value arg=value ...`, one alternative
# per `XlsxMutation` variant, every keyword/arg-name token copied from the real `format!(...)` call sites.
#
# `set-snapshot`'s `snapshot` and `set-cell`/`remove-cell`'s `address` carry the lowercase hex of the
# value's RFC 8259 JSON (`enc_xlsx_snapshot`/`enc_cell_address`: `enc_str(dsl::json::to_json_string(..))`),
# so both are the framework's built-in `hex` MACRO (bare `hex`, deliberately not defined as a production --
# `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall 2). `[0]`/`[1,x]` is `encode_option`'s tri-state shape (§1.4).
document = set-snapshot | insert-sheet | remove-sheet | rename-sheet | set-cell | remove-cell | insert-shared-string | remove-shared-string | set-shared-string

set-snapshot = "set-snapshot" "snapshot" "=" hex
insert-sheet = "insert-sheet" "sheet" "=" sheet
remove-sheet = "remove-sheet" "name" "=" hex
rename-sheet = "rename-sheet" "name" "=" hex "new-name" "=" hex
set-cell = "set-cell" "address" "=" hex "value" "=" cell-value
remove-cell = "remove-cell" "address" "=" hex
insert-shared-string = "insert-shared-string" "value" "=" hex
remove-shared-string = "remove-shared-string" "index" "=" INT
set-shared-string = "set-shared-string" "index" "=" INT "value" "=" hex

# ── `XlsxSheet` -- `[name,[cells]]` (`enc_sheet`) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
sheet = "[" hex "," "[" cell-list? "]" "]"
cell-list = cell {"," cell}*
cell = "[" INT "," INT "," cell-value "]"

# ── `XlsxCellValue` (`enc_cell_value`) -- single-letter tag immediately followed by the bracketed
# positional payload: `N`umber, `S`hared-string index, `I`nline string, `B`oolean, e`R`ror, `F`ormula
# with its optional cached value, `E`mpty. ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cell-value = "N" "[" number "]" | "S" "[" INT "]" | "I" "[" hex "]" | "B" "[" bool-lit "]" | "R" "[" hex "]" | "F" "[" hex "," opt-cell-value "]" | "E" "[" "]"
opt-cell-value = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," cell-value "]"
bool-lit = "0" | "1"
number = INT | FLOAT

number = INT / FLOAT / IDENT

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.pdf.diff
start diff
comment none

# P2-FG3: real one-line `DiffCodec::print_diff`/`parse_diff` shape for `stdio.pdf` (1.4)'s
# hand-rolled `PdfDiff` (../../🦀️.rs). Every keyword/tag token and every value
# micro-syntax production below is copied verbatim from that file's own `format!(...)` call sites
# (`enc_pages_diff`/`enc_page_diff`/`enc_page`/`enc_str`), never guessed — the same way the sibling
# 1.7 standard's own diff grammar is written.
#
# `PdfDiff` has exactly one top-level field, `pages`, because that is the whole of what a 1.4
# snapshot carries (`../../📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs`: schema + the document's page tree). An
# unchanged document prints as the empty line, so `diff` is `pages-field?`.
diff = pages-field?
pages-field = "pages" "=" pages-diff-body

# `enc_pages_diff`/`dec_pages_diff` — the index-keyed collection triple (`📖️grammar-recipe.md`
# §1.4): `[removed];[modified];[added]`. `modified` items carry a sparse `PdfPageDiff`, `added`
# items carry a whole `PageDoc`.
pages-diff-body = "[" removed-index-item* "]" ";" "[" page-modified-item* "]" ";" "[" page-added-item* "]"
removed-index-item = INT ","?
page-modified-item = INT ":" page-diff-lit ","?
page-added-item = INT ":" page-lit ","?

# `enc_page_diff`/`dec_page_diff` — `PdfPageDiff`'s own sparse fields as single-letter `tag:value`
# pairs: `W`=width, `H`=height, `X`=text (hex, so a page's text may carry any byte including this
# grammar's own separators).
page-diff-lit = "[" page-diff-item* "]"
page-diff-item = page-diff-entry ","?
page-diff-entry = "W" ":" number | "H" ":" number | "X" ":" hex

# `enc_page`/`dec_page` — a whole `PageDoc`: `[width,height,hex(text)]`. Both dimensions print via
# bare Rust `Display`, so a whole-valued one prints with no fractional part (hence `INT | FLOAT`,
# the same defensive convention stl's and obj's own `number` productions use).
page-lit = "[" number "," number "," hex "]"
number = INT | FLOAT

declaration-lit = "[" hex "," opt-hex "," opt-bool "," bool-lit "]"
opt-doctype = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," doctype-lit "]"

dtd-declaration = "E" "[" bool-lit "," hex "," hex "]"

# `enc_node_diff`/`dec_node_diff` -- `XmlNodeDiff` itself needs a tag (`E`=Element, `T`=Text,
# `R`=Replace) since, unlike a bare `XmlNode`, it appears standalone (not always inside a bracketed
# container) at the top-level `root=` token position. Genuinely recursive: `E`'s children slot
# references `node-diff` (via `child-modified-item`) which references `node-diff` back through
# `children-diff-body` -- the same self-recursion `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(g) documents as

attr-modified-item = hex ":" hex ","?
attr-added-item = hex ":" hex ","?

# `enc_children_diff`/`dec_children_diff` -- `[removed];[modified];[added]`, index-keyed.
children-diff-body = "[" child-removed-item* "]" ";" "[" child-modified-item* "]" ";" "[" child-added-item* "]"
child-removed-item = INT ","?
child-modified-item = INT ":" node-diff ","?
child-added-item = INT ":" xml-node ","?

node-item = xml-node ","?
attr-order-item = hex ","?

# P2-P3: `stdio.txt`'s real DSL text form (🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs
# `ArtifactDsl::print_dsl` -> `store::semio_format::wrap_text`) is the mandatory preamble line,
# a newline, then the ENTIRE remaining document body VERBATIM: `TxtSnapshot::to_body()` is
# arbitrary UTF-8 text, not itself a line-structured grammar (a `stdio.txt` document literally
# IS "a text file" -- Phase 1's own final-gate audit already called this artifact's old,
# unparseable ABNF placeholder the single most CONCEPTUALLY accurate handcrafted grammar in the
# whole stdio set; this file ports that same precision into the real, parseable dialect). Uses
# M1's `REST` raw-span terminal (P2-M1 report, Item 2: `Symbol::Terminal("REST")` -- reads the
# ORIGINAL source text from the current byte offset to EOF, past whatever the shared lexer
# already fragmented into tokens, so it correctly captures a body containing characters outside
# this dialect's fixed token alphabet) -- the ONE primitive built for exactly this whole-body
# capture case.
comment none

# `dsl::fixture_sweep::m5_handcrafted_grammar_conformance::dsl_body_from_fixture` (and this
# artifact's own `grammar_conformance_law`, mirroring it) feeds the Recognizer
# `"<envelope-id>\n<body>"` -- the full `"semio {plugin}.{artifact}.{component} v{n}"` preamble
# line is a FRAMEWORK-level envelope concern, already described once at
# 🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🧬️semio/📡️protocol/📡️.protocol.semio (P2-M3
# deliverable 3) and stripped down to the bare `SemioEnvelope::envelope_id()` (`"stdio.txt"`)
# before this grammar ever sees it -- same convention every sibling artifact's own snapshot
# grammar already uses (e.g. csv's `envelope-mark = "stdio.csv"`).
document = envelope-mark body
envelope-mark = "stdio.txt"

# The rest of the file, byte-for-byte, past the envelope mark's own trailing newline.
# `wrap_text` (🧬️semio/🦀️.rs) `trim_start()`s the body before gluing it after the real
# preamble, so a genuine `print_dsl` output never has leading blank lines here -- `REST`'s own
# first captured byte lands exactly on the body's real first character (see
# `codec_retention_law`'s own doc comment, ⚙️engine/🦀️.rs, for the one pre-existing,
# out-of-ownership-boundary lossy case this framework behavior has: a body that legitimately
# STARTS with its own blank line).
body = REST

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.txt.diff
start diff

# P2-P3: real one-line `print_diff`/`parse_diff` form -- `TxtDiff` derives `dsl::DslDiff`, whose
# `DiffCodec::print_diff` is `dsl::print(&self.__dsl_diff_to_record(), &Self::__dsl_diff_spec(),
# dsl::JoinMode::Inline)` -- the SAME generic derive-driven printer the sibling mutations grammar
# (../../🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio) documents, applied here to a STRUCT
# instead of an enum: no leading keyword at all (`TxtDiff::__dsl_diff_spec()`'s own
# `RecordSpec::keyword` is `None`, since no `#[dsl(keyword = "...")]` container attribute is set
# -- every field prints as a bare `key=value`/`key=<nested-fields>` run). Every top-level field is
# `Option<T>` (present = changed, absent = unchanged); an all-`None` diff prints as the empty
# string (verified: `TxtDiff::default().print_diff() == ""`).
comment none

diff = trailing-newline-field? line-ending-field? lines-field?
trailing-newline-field = "trailing-newline" "=" bit
line-ending-field = "line-ending" "=" line-ending-value
bit = "true" | "false"
line-ending-value = "lf" | "cr-lf"

# `TxtLinesDiff` is itself a `#[derive(dsl::DslRecord)]` struct with no container keyword either
# -- printed as a flat run of its own 3 keyed fields directly after `lines=`, with no wrapping
# delimiter of its own (only the `[...]` lists below are self-delimiting; the normative apply
# order -- modified, then removed descending, then added ascending clamped to `min(index,len)` --
# is documented on `TxtLinesDiff` itself, ../../🔺️diff/🦀️.rs, not repeated here).
lines-field = "lines" "=" lines-diff
lines-diff = removed-field modified-field added-field
removed-field = "removed" "=" "[" INT* "]"
modified-field = "modified" "=" "[" line-modified-entry* "]"
added-field = "added" "=" "[" line-added-entry* "]"

# `TxtLineModified`/`TxtLineAdded` are likewise keyword-less `#[derive(dsl::DslRecord)]` structs
# -- each list ITEM prints as its own flat `index=<N> text=<value>` run, back to back with no
# item separator (list-of-record boundary recovery is structural: the next item's own `index=`
# key marks where the previous item ended -- the SAME "next real field's own leading key IS the
# boundary" pattern the sibling mutations grammar's `snapshot-fields` sequence already relies on).
line-modified-entry = "index" "=" INT "text" "=" text-value
line-added-entry = "index" "=" INT "text" "=" text-value
text-value = IDENT | TEXT

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.stl.diff
extension stl
start document

# FG1: real `DiffCodec::print_diff`/`parse_diff` shape — F6's hand-rolled `print_stl_diff`/
# `parse_stl_diff` (🔺️diff/🦀️.rs), replacing the F6-era placeholder that described a
# serde-JSON `{"solidName":..., "triangles":{...}}` wire object the codec never emits (F6 reverted
# the `dsl::DslDiff` derive after a real, reproduced `dsl`-grammar bug on the doubly-nested
# `vertices: [[f64;3];3]` field — see this file's module doc comment / `f6-stl-report.md` for the
# full citation; a shared-framework bug, out of this wave's ownership boundary). Sparse: at most one
# `solid-name=<hex>` token, then at most one `triangles{...}` collection-triple token, SPACE
# separated (never comma — `print_stl_diff`'s own `tokens.join(" ")`), absent field = unchanged
# (never emitted as an empty/null marker). `triangles` is index-keyed (INT keys) — same
# `[removed];[modified];[added]` 3-section collection-triple shape png's own `text-chunks-clause`
# uses (this dialect's recipe §1.4).
document = solid-name-field? triangles-field?

solid-name-field = "solid-name" "=" hex

triangles-field = "triangles" "{" "[" removed-list? "]" ";" "[" modified-list? "]" ";" "[" added-list? "]" "}"
removed-list = INT {"," INT}*
modified-list = modified-item {"," modified-item}*
modified-item = INT ":" triangle-diff-value
added-list = added-item {"," added-item}*
added-item = INT ":" triangle-value

# `enc_triangle_diff`'s own sparse tag list — `N:<vec3>` and/or `V:<vertices>`, comma-joined,
# either/both present (never both omitted when the outer `modified` entry itself is emitted —
# `triangle_diff_is_empty` guards that upstream in Rust, but this grammar stays permissive, matching
# every other pilot's own permissive-superset convention: a grammar recognizing MORE than the
# encoder ever emits is fine, recognizing less is the real bug class this recipe guards against).
triangle-diff-value = "[" diff-tag-list? "]"
diff-tag-list = diff-tag {"," diff-tag}*
diff-tag = normal-tag | vertices-tag
normal-tag = "N" ":" vec3-value
vertices-tag = "V" ":" vertices-value

# `enc_triangle`/`enc_vertices`/`enc_vec3` — every array level gets its own `[...]` bracket (the
# depth marker `dsl`'s own flat `Shape::Tuple` printer is missing for `[[f64;3];3]`), which is
# exactly what sidesteps that bug: `split_top_level`'s bracket-depth-aware comma split recovers
# nesting unambiguously. Reused verbatim by the sibling `../../🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️component.
# grammar.semio`'s own `triangle-value`/`vertices-value`/`vec3-value` (same intra-artifact primitive
# reuse `svg`'s `SvgMutation` uses over `SvgDiff`'s own).
triangle-value = "[" vec3-value "," vertices-value "]"
vertices-value = "[" vec3-value "," vec3-value "," vec3-value "]"
vec3-value = "[" number "," number "," number "]"

# `f64` values print via Rust's `Display` (`{}`), which never emits a trailing `.0` for a
# whole-numbered float — a coordinate lexes as INT whenever its value happens to be integral, FLOAT
# otherwise. Same `INT | FLOAT` idiom json's own `number` production uses, for the identical reason.
number = INT | FLOAT

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.stl.mutations
extension stl
start document

# FG1: real `OpText::print_op`/`parse_op` shape — F6's hand-rolled `print_stl_op`/`parse_stl_op`
# (🧬️mutations/🦀️.rs), replacing the F6-era placeholder that described a serde-JSON
# `{"mutation":"...", ...}` wire struct the codec never emits (F6 reverted the `dsl::DslOps` derive
# after a real, reproduced `dsl`-grammar bug — see `f6-stl-report.md` and this artifact's own
# `🧬️mutations`/`🔺️diff` module doc comments for the full root-cause citation; out of this wave's
# ownership boundary to fix). One keyword line, space-separated `key=value` tokens, every variant's
# args ALWAYS present (no sparse omission, unlike the sibling diff grammar). Every keyword/field-key
# token below is copied verbatim from `print_stl_op`'s real match arms, not invented:
#   set-snapshot snapshot=[<hex>,<hex>,[<triangle>,...]]
#   set-solid-name name=<hex>
#   insert-triangle index=<INT> triangle=[<vec3>,<vertices>]
#   remove-triangle index=<INT>
#   set-triangle-normal index=<INT> normal=<vec3>
#   set-triangle-vertices index=<INT> vertices=<vertices>
# `name`/`solid_name`/`schema` (inside `snapshot=`) are lowercase hex (`hex_encode_str`) — the
# mandatory `hex` MACRO (bare `hex`, no matching production — `Symbol::Ref` falls back
# production-then-macro), never a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*` (P2-P1-fix Bug 3). `normal`/`vertices`/
# `triangle`/`snapshot`'s numeric payload reuses the exact `[...]`-bracketed grammar
# `🔺️diff::component`'s `enc_vec3`/`enc_vertices`/`enc_triangle` primitives emit — every array level
# gets its own bracket (the depth marker `dsl`'s own flat `Shape::Tuple` printer is missing), which
# is exactly what sidesteps that bug: `split_top_level`'s bracket-depth-aware comma split recovers
# nesting unambiguously.
document = set-snapshot | set-solid-name | insert-triangle | remove-triangle | set-triangle-normal | set-triangle-vertices

set-snapshot = "set-snapshot" "snapshot" "=" snapshot-value
set-solid-name = "set-solid-name" "name" "=" hex
insert-triangle = "insert-triangle" "index" "=" INT "triangle" "=" triangle-value
remove-triangle = "remove-triangle" "index" "=" INT
set-triangle-normal = "set-triangle-normal" "index" "=" INT "normal" "=" vec3-value
set-triangle-vertices = "set-triangle-vertices" "index" "=" INT "vertices" "=" vertices-value

# `🔺️diff::component`'s own primitives don't need (only `SetSnapshot`'s payload does), defined in
# `🧬️mutations::component`'s own `enc_snapshot`/`dec_snapshot`.
snapshot-value = "[" hex "," hex "," "[" triangle-list? "]" "]"
triangle-list = triangle-value {"," triangle-value}*

# `enc_triangle`/`enc_vertices`/`enc_vec3` — copied verbatim from `🔺️diff::component`'s own value

triangle-value = "[" vec3-value "," vertices-value "]"
vertices-value = "[" vec3-value "," vec3-value "," vec3-value "]"
vec3-value = "[" number "," number "," number "]"
number = INT | FLOAT

# Direct identities: set-snapshot, set-version-info.
#
# `DwgMutation`'s OpText is the SHARED canonical-JSON op codec
# (`impl_serde_op_codec!(DwgMutation, "dwg-mutation")`, 📇️registry/🧬️contract/🦀️.rs): `print_op` is
# `pack::json_to_string(json_from_dsl_value(to_value(self)))` and nothing else, so the real wire of
# every kind is one internally-tagged JSON object — `{"mutation":"setSnapshot","snapshot":{…}}` /
# `{"mutation":"setVersionInfo","version":…,"maintenanceVersion":…,"codepage":…}` — with
# `#[value(tag = "mutation", rename_all = "camelCase")]` fixing the discriminant key and the
# camelCase kind spellings. A grammar is a DESCRIPTION of that printer, so it describes JSON. The
# version this replaced described a keyword-and-record op text (`"set-snapshot" "snapshot" record`,
# kebab kinds, `IDENT "="` fields) that no printer in this crate has emitted since the shared codec
# landed, and `ops_grammar_conformance_law` failed on the very first case.
#
# The discriminant is NOT spelled as a literal production here: literals in this dialect match a
# token's text, and `"mutation"` would match the bare IDENT `mutation`, never the quoted member name
# the JSON wire actually carries — the two kinds are enumerated above instead, the way the sibling
# 📸️jpg/📷️png mutation grammars enumerate theirs. `kinds_match_enum_and_catalog`
# (🧬️mutations/🧪️tests) is what keeps that list honest against the enum and both oracle catalogs.
#
# Dialect notes carried over from the 🧾️json artifact's own snapshot grammar (same lexer):
# comma-repeated tails group with `{...}*`, never `(...)*` (bare parens are macro-call syntax);
# a production may not be named `string`/`extension`/`use`/`start`/`comment` (header directives);
# `string double backslash` turns on JSON escape decoding for every TEXT token; whitespace is lexer
# trivia, so no `ws` production is needed.
dialect grammar
grammar stdio.dwg.ac1024.mutations
start op
comment none
string double backslash

op = object

value = object | array | json-string | number | "true" | "false" | "null"

object = "{" "}" | "{" member {"," member}* "}"
member = json-string ":" value

array = "[" "]" | "[" value {"," value}* "]"

json-string = TEXT

number = INT | FLOAT

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.dxf.diff
extension dxf
start document

# P2-FG1: real one-line `DiffCodec::print_diff`/`parse_diff` shape ALREADY emitted by
# `../🦀️.rs`'s `print_dxf_diff`/`parse_dxf_diff` — zero or more space-separated
# `key=[removed];[modified];[added]`-shaped tokens (`header-vars=`/`tables=`/`blocks=`/`entities=`,
# the real four `DxfDiff` fields; `schema` is identity-only and never diffed). `document = diff-token*`
# naturally matches the empty line too (`Symbol::Star` matches zero occurrences, and an empty
# `parse_diff("")` input lexes to zero tokens, so `recognize`'s `pos == tokens.len()` check passes
# trivially) — no separate empty-line alternative needed, same shape `stdio.json`'s own diff
# grammar's `document` production relies on.
#
# Every collection triple below (`removed-*-list`/`modified-*-list`/`added-*-list`) mirrors the
# recipe's own copy-pasteable collection-triple shape (§1.4): `[removed]` / `[modified]` / `[added]`,
# joined by literal `;`, each independently `[...]`-bracketed — verbatim from `enc_name_triple`/
# `enc_index_triple` in `../🦀️.rs`'s `#region 🔖️CollectionTripleCodecs`. Name-keyed
# collections (`header-vars`/`layers`/`styles`/`linetypes`) key `removed`/`modified` by the item's
# hex-encoded NAME; index-keyed collections (`entities`, both top-level and a block's own nested
# `entities`, plus `blocks` itself) key everything by `INT`. `added` entries are always keyed by the
# FINAL-position index for BOTH shapes (`enc_name_triple`'s own `added_s` uses `i:enc_item(t)` where
# `i` is the added-entry's target index, matching `DxfHeaderVarAdded.index`/etc — not the name).
#
# Every `Option<T>` diff field uses the recipe's `[0]`/`[1,<value>]` tri-state tag pair
# (`encode_option`/`decode_option`, `../🦀️.rs`'s `#region 🔖️Primitives`) — one `opt-*`
# production per payload shape, reused across every diff struct that carries that shape.
#
# `entity-diff`'s `Replace` arm carries a WHOLE `dxf-entity` (tag-inside-a-tag, unambiguous since
# the outer bracket always closes the inner one first) for the plan's "Replace on kind change"
# rule applied to an enum collection element — same convention `stdio.json`'s `JsonValueDiff`
# grammar and every other pilot's kind-changing diff arm uses.
document = diff-token*
diff-token = header-vars-tok | tables-tok | blocks-tok | entities-tok

header-vars-tok = "header-vars" "=" removed-hv-list ";" modified-hv-list ";" added-hv-list
tables-tok = "tables" "=" tables-diff-payload
blocks-tok = "blocks" "=" removed-blk-list ";" modified-blk-list ";" added-blk-list
entities-tok = "entities" "=" removed-ent-list ";" modified-ent-list ";" added-ent-list

# `enc_f64` (`format!("{v}")`) prints a bare decimal, lexing as `INT` (no `.`) or `FLOAT` (has `.`).
num = INT | FLOAT
point3 = "[" num "," num "," num "]"
points4 = "[" point3 "," point3 "," point3 "," point3 "]"

# `enc_dxf_value`/`dec_dxf_value` — `S[hex]`/`I[digits]`/`D[float]`/`P[x,y,z]`.
dxf-value = "S" "[" hex "]" | "I" "[" INT "]" | "D" "[" num "]" | "P" "[" num "," num "," num "]"
group-code = "[" INT "," dxf-value "]"
group-codes = "[" "]" | "[" group-code {"," group-code}* "]"

vertex = "[" num "," num "," num "," num "," group-codes "]"
vertex-list = "[" "]" | "[" vertex {"," vertex}* "]"

# `enc_dxf_entity`/`dec_dxf_entity` — one tag letter per typed `DxfEntity` variant (used both by
# `entity-diff`'s `Replace` arm and every collection's `added` full-item payload).
dxf-entity = "L" "[" point3 "," point3 "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "C" "[" point3 "," num "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "A" "[" point3 "," num "," num "," num "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "W" "[" vertex-list "," INT "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "T" "[" point3 "," num "," hex "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "S" "[" points4 "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "I" "[" hex "," point3 "," point3 "," num "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "O" "[" hex "," group-codes "]"
entity-list = "[" "]" | "[" dxf-entity {"," dxf-entity}* "]"

header-var = "[" hex "," INT "," dxf-value "," group-codes "]"
layer-item = "[" hex "," INT "," hex "," INT "," group-codes "]"
style-item = "[" hex "," INT "," hex "," group-codes "]"
linetype-item = "[" hex "," INT "," hex "," group-codes "]"
block-item = "[" hex "," point3 "," entity-list "," group-codes "]"

# Tri-state `Option<T>` wrappers — `[0]` (unchanged/None) or `[1,<value>]` (Some).
opt-int = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," INT "]"
opt-num = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," num "]"
opt-hex = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," hex "]"
opt-value = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," dxf-value "]"
opt-group-codes = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," group-codes "]"
opt-point3 = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," point3 "]"
opt-points4 = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," points4 "]"
opt-vertex-list = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," vertex-list "]"

header-var-diff = "[" opt-int "," opt-value "," opt-group-codes "]"
layer-diff = "[" opt-int "," opt-hex "," opt-int "," opt-group-codes "]"
style-diff = "[" opt-int "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]"
linetype-diff = "[" opt-int "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]"

# `enc_entity_diff`/`dec_entity_diff` — `R`=Replace (carries a whole `dxf-entity`), else one
# kind-specific field-diff arm per typed entity kind, same letters `dxf-entity` uses.
entity-diff = "R" "[" dxf-entity "]" | "L" "[" opt-point3 "," opt-point3 "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]" | "C" "[" opt-point3 "," opt-num "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]" | "A" "[" opt-point3 "," opt-num "," opt-num "," opt-num "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]" | "W" "[" opt-vertex-list "," opt-int "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]" | "T" "[" opt-point3 "," opt-num "," opt-hex "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]" | "S" "[" opt-points4 "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]" | "I" "[" opt-hex "," opt-point3 "," opt-point3 "," opt-num "," opt-hex "," opt-group-codes "]" | "O" "[" opt-group-codes "]"

# Index-keyed entity collection triple — reused verbatim at TWO tree depths: the top-level
# `entities=` token AND a block's own nested `entities` sub-diff (`opt-entities-diff` below).
removed-ent-list = "[" "]" | "[" INT {"," INT}* "]"
ent-modified = INT ":" entity-diff
modified-ent-list = "[" "]" | "[" ent-modified {"," ent-modified}* "]"
ent-added = INT ":" dxf-entity
added-ent-list = "[" "]" | "[" ent-added {"," ent-added}* "]"
opt-entities-diff = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," removed-ent-list ";" modified-ent-list ";" added-ent-list "]"

block-diff = "[" opt-hex "," opt-point3 "," opt-entities-diff "," opt-group-codes "]"

# Index-keyed block collection triple (top-level `blocks=` token only — a block never nests
# another block in R12).
removed-blk-list = "[" "]" | "[" INT {"," INT}* "]"
blk-modified = INT ":" block-diff
modified-blk-list = "[" "]" | "[" blk-modified {"," blk-modified}* "]"
blk-added = INT ":" block-item
added-blk-list = "[" "]" | "[" blk-added {"," blk-added}* "]"

# Name-keyed collection triples — `header-vars`/`layers`/`styles`/`linetypes`, each removed/modified
# keyed by the item's hex-encoded name, added keyed by the item's FINAL-position `INT` index.
removed-hv-list = "[" "]" | "[" hex {"," hex}* "]"
hv-modified = hex ":" header-var-diff
modified-hv-list = "[" "]" | "[" hv-modified {"," hv-modified}* "]"
hv-added = INT ":" header-var
added-hv-list = "[" "]" | "[" hv-added {"," hv-added}* "]"

removed-layer-list = "[" "]" | "[" hex {"," hex}* "]"
layer-modified = hex ":" layer-diff
modified-layer-list = "[" "]" | "[" layer-modified {"," layer-modified}* "]"
layer-added = INT ":" layer-item
added-layer-list = "[" "]" | "[" layer-added {"," layer-added}* "]"

removed-style-list = "[" "]" | "[" hex {"," hex}* "]"
style-modified = hex ":" style-diff
modified-style-list = "[" "]" | "[" style-modified {"," style-modified}* "]"
style-added = INT ":" style-item
added-style-list = "[" "]" | "[" style-added {"," style-added}* "]"

removed-linetype-list = "[" "]" | "[" hex {"," hex}* "]"
linetype-modified = hex ":" linetype-diff
modified-linetype-list = "[" "]" | "[" linetype-modified {"," linetype-modified}* "]"
linetype-added = INT ":" linetype-item
added-linetype-list = "[" "]" | "[" linetype-added {"," linetype-added}* "]"

# `DxfTablesDiff` is a plain per-field `Option<...>` struct (one opt per name-keyed sub-collection),
# not itself a collection triple — `enc_tables_diff`'s own bracketed 3-tuple shape.
opt-layers-diff = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," removed-layer-list ";" modified-layer-list ";" added-layer-list "]"
opt-styles-diff = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," removed-style-list ";" modified-style-list ";" added-style-list "]"
opt-linetypes-diff = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," removed-linetype-list ";" modified-linetype-list ";" added-linetype-list "]"
tables-diff-payload = "[" opt-layers-diff "," opt-styles-diff "," opt-linetypes-diff "]"

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.dxf.mutations
extension dxf
start document

# P2-FG1: real one-line `OpText::print_op`/`parse_op` shape ALREADY emitted by
# `🏅️standards/🔖️r12/🪆️subsets/📰️header/🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🦀️.rs`'s `print_dxf_mutation`/
# `parse_dxf_mutation` (`keyword arg=value ...`, space-separated, `=`-joined tokens — F6's own
# hand-rolled convention, reusing `🔺️diff`'s `pub(crate)` item-literal encoders `enc_header_var`/
# `enc_layer`/`enc_style`/`enc_linetype`/`enc_dxf_entity`/`enc_block`/`enc_dxf_snapshot` verbatim,
# per that file's own module doc comment). Every keyword/field-name literal below is copied from
# the real `format!(...)`/`match keyword` call sites, not invented.
#
# `hex` (bare `hex`, deliberately NOT a production in this file) is the framework's built-in `hex`
# MACRO (`📖️grammar/🦀️.rs`'s `default_macros`) — `Symbol::Ref` falls back
# production→macro, `Recognizer::match_macro_span` tries the largest token span first and
# backtracks correctly, which is why a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*` production is wrong here (P2
# recipe pitfall #2: a hex run mixing digits/letters fragments across INT/IDENT tokens at the
# lexer level, and a naive Star has no backtracking to stop short of a following bareword literal
# — `hex` the macro handles both, validated end-to-end by this file's own `ops_grammar_conformance_law`).
#
# Every nested item literal below (`header-var`/`layer-item`/`style-item`/`linetype-item`/
# `dxf-entity`/`block-item`/`dxf-snapshot`) mirrors `🔺️diff/🦀️.rs`'s real `enc_*`/`dec_*`
# functions field-for-field, in the SAME positional order those functions emit — see that file's
# `#region 🔖️ItemCodecs`/`#region 🔖️EntityValueCodecs`. `dxf-entity`'s 8-arm tag-prefixed shape
# (`L`=Line,`C`=Circle,`A`=Arc,`W`=Polyline,`T`=Text,`S`=Solid,`I`=Insert,`O`=Other) is bounded, not
# self-recursive — a `block-item`'s own `entity-list` references `dxf-entity`, but no `DxfEntity`
# variant nests another `DxfEntity` (R12 has no entity-in-entity nesting), so this whole grammar
# has a fixed maximum depth, genuinely exercised end-to-end (incl. every entity kind, a POLYLINE
# with vertices, and a `SetSnapshot` payload nesting a block-with-entity) by
# `ops_grammar_conformance_law` against real `print_op` output for every `DxfMutation` variant.
document = set-snapshot | set-header-var | remove-header-var | insert-layer | remove-layer | set-layer | insert-style | remove-style | set-style | insert-linetype | remove-linetype | set-linetype | insert-entity | remove-entity | set-entity | insert-block | remove-block | set-block

set-snapshot = "set-snapshot" "snapshot" "=" dxf-snapshot

set-header-var = "set-header-var" "name" "=" hex "header-var" "=" header-var
remove-header-var = "remove-header-var" "name" "=" hex

insert-layer = "insert-layer" "index" "=" INT "layer" "=" layer-item
remove-layer = "remove-layer" "name" "=" hex
set-layer = "set-layer" "name" "=" hex "layer" "=" layer-item

insert-style = "insert-style" "index" "=" INT "style" "=" style-item
remove-style = "remove-style" "name" "=" hex
set-style = "set-style" "name" "=" hex "style" "=" style-item

insert-linetype = "insert-linetype" "index" "=" INT "linetype" "=" linetype-item
remove-linetype = "remove-linetype" "name" "=" hex
set-linetype = "set-linetype" "name" "=" hex "linetype" "=" linetype-item

insert-entity = "insert-entity" "index" "=" INT "entity" "=" dxf-entity
remove-entity = "remove-entity" "index" "=" INT
set-entity = "set-entity" "index" "=" INT "entity" "=" dxf-entity

insert-block = "insert-block" "index" "=" INT "block" "=" block-item
remove-block = "remove-block" "index" "=" INT
set-block = "set-block" "index" "=" INT "block" "=" block-item

# `enc_f64` (`format!("{v}")`) prints a bare decimal, lexing as `INT` (no `.`) or `FLOAT` (has `.`).
num = INT | FLOAT
point3 = "[" num "," num "," num "]"
points4 = "[" point3 "," point3 "," point3 "," point3 "]"

# `enc_dxf_value`/`dec_dxf_value` — `S[hex]`/`I[digits]`/`D[float]`/`P[x,y,z]`.
dxf-value = "S" "[" hex "]" | "I" "[" INT "]" | "D" "[" num "]" | "P" "[" num "," num "," num "]"
group-code = "[" INT "," dxf-value "]"
group-codes = "[" "]" | "[" group-code {"," group-code}* "]"

vertex = "[" num "," num "," num "," num "," group-codes "]"
vertex-list = "[" "]" | "[" vertex {"," vertex}* "]"

# `enc_dxf_entity`/`dec_dxf_entity` — one tag letter per typed `DxfEntity` variant.
dxf-entity = "L" "[" point3 "," point3 "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "C" "[" point3 "," num "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "A" "[" point3 "," num "," num "," num "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "W" "[" vertex-list "," INT "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "T" "[" point3 "," num "," hex "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "S" "[" points4 "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "I" "[" hex "," point3 "," point3 "," num "," hex "," group-codes "]" | "O" "[" hex "," group-codes "]"
entity-list = "[" "]" | "[" dxf-entity {"," dxf-entity}* "]"

header-var = "[" hex "," INT "," dxf-value "," group-codes "]"
header-var-list = "[" "]" | "[" header-var {"," header-var}* "]"

layer-item = "[" hex "," INT "," hex "," INT "," group-codes "]"
layer-list = "[" "]" | "[" layer-item {"," layer-item}* "]"

style-item = "[" hex "," INT "," hex "," group-codes "]"
style-list = "[" "]" | "[" style-item {"," style-item}* "]"

linetype-item = "[" hex "," INT "," hex "," group-codes "]"
linetype-list = "[" "]" | "[" linetype-item {"," linetype-item}* "]"

block-item = "[" hex "," point3 "," entity-list "," group-codes "]"
block-list = "[" "]" | "[" block-item {"," block-item}* "]"

dxf-tag-list = "[" "]" | "[" dxf-tag {"," dxf-tag}* "]"
other-table = "[" hex "," dxf-tag-list "]"
other-table-list = "[" "]" | "[" other-table {"," other-table}* "]"

dxf-tables = "[" layer-list "," style-list "," linetype-list "]"

# `enc_dxf_snapshot`/`dec_dxf_snapshot` — the WHOLE snapshot, only reachable via `SetSnapshot`'s
# own payload (`🔺️diff/🦀️.rs`'s own doc comment on `enc_dxf_snapshot` names this exactly).
dxf-snapshot = "[" hex "," header-var-list "," dxf-tables "," other-table-list "," block-list "," entity-list "]"
