dialect grammar
grammar stdio.tiff.snapshot
extension tiff
start document

# TIFF has no textual syntax of its own — `store::ArtifactDsl::print_dsl`/`parse_dsl`
# (../../🦀️.rs, the `HandcraftedArtifactCodecs` region) hex-encode/decode the REAL
# binary TIFF 6.0 file bytes (byte-order mark + IFD chain, TIFF6 §2) verbatim, byte-for-byte —
# this is png's own honest precedent from Phase 1's survey (P2-W0 §1b: "hex-dump grammar per
# png's own precedent"), not an aspiration. See ../💾️binary/📡️.protocol.semio for that
# same binary's real structural grammar (runtime-endian header + first-IFD entry table).
comment none

# `dsl::fixture_sweep`'s `dsl_body_from_fixture` feeds the Recognizer
# "<envelope-id>\n<body>" (`SemioEnvelope::envelope_id` = "stdio.tiff", the real preamble
# line's own trailing "v<n>" already stripped by the harness) — the shared lexer treats the
# preamble's newline as trivia, so `envelope-mark` and the hex body sit directly adjacent in
# the significant token stream, matching json/csv/png's own grammars' identical convention.
envelope-mark = "stdio.tiff"
document = envelope-mark hex-body

# The rest of the DSL text is one lowercase-hex digit run — the real TIFF file's bytes (8-byte
# header + IFD chain + generic tag/type/value entries + strip pixel data), hex-encoded
# losslessly (`encode_tiff`/`decode_tiff`, ⚙️engine/🦀️.rs). `hex` (bare `hex`,
# deliberately NOT defined as a production here) is the framework's built-in `hex` MACRO
# (`📖️grammar/🦀️.rs`'s `default_macros`/`macro_hex_ok`) — the dialect-recipe's own
# documented rule (`📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall 2): a hand-rolled
# `{INT | IDENT}*`-shaped production would silently mis-lex a `<digits>e<digits>` byte run as
# one FLOAT token instead of alternating INT/IDENT; the macro's own largest-span-first
# backtracking (`Recognizer::match_macro_span`) handles it correctly with no grammar-file
# workaround needed — same mechanism json's/csv's/png's own `hex` doc comments already document
# for their op/diff payloads.
hex-body = hex

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.tiff.diff
extension tiff
start document
comment none

# P2-FG2: real one-line `DiffCodec::print_diff`/`parse_diff` shape ALREADY emitted by
# `../../🦀️.rs` (`print_tiff_diff`/`parse_tiff_diff`), replacing the F6-era placeholder
# that described neither the real snapshot NOR the real diff wire shape. Every keyword/tag token
# below is copied verbatim from the real `format!(...)` call sites, not invented.
#
# `comment none`: not strictly required by any token this grammar's own alphabet produces (hex
# payloads are lowercase-only, never containing `#`), kept for consistency with the sibling
# ../../📸️snapshot/📝️text grammar.
#
# `hex` (bare `hex`, referenced below but deliberately NOT defined as a production in this file)
# is the framework's built-in `hex` MACRO — see the mandatory-macro rationale in
# `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall 2 (a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*` production never
# backtracks and would silently swallow a following bareword literal like `ifds`/`pixels`).
document = byte-order-tok? ifds-tok? pixels-tok?
byte-order-tok = "byte-order" "=" byte-order-lit
byte-order-lit = "0" | "1"
ifds-tok = "ifds" "=" ifds-diff-body
pixels-tok = "pixels" "=" hex

# `enc_ifds_diff`/`dec_ifds_diff` -- `[removed];[modified];[added]`, index-keyed (TIFF's own IFD

ifd-added-list = ifd-added-item {"," ifd-added-item}*

# `added` entries are `tag:kind:values` (colon-separated -- safe since `kind` is bare decimal and
# `values` never contains a literal `:`).

tag-modified-list = tag-modified-item {"," tag-modified-item}*
tag-modified-item = INT ":" INT ":" tiff-values
tag-added-list = tag-added-item {"," tag-added-item}*
tag-added-item = INT ":" INT ":" tiff-values

ifd-entries = "[" ifd-entry-list? "]"

# bracketed positional payload (same convention `xml`'s `enc_xml_node`/gif's enum codecs use):

# `cargo test -p semio-s-plugin-stdio --lib artifacts::deflate -- --ignored --nocapture` run of a

# P2-FG3: real one-line `print_diff`/`parse_diff` form this artifact's hand-rolled `DiffCodec`
# ACTUALLY emits (../🦀️.rs `print_gltf_diff`/`parse_gltf_diff`) -- a space-separated
# `name=value` token per changed top-level field, in `GltfDiff`'s own struct declaration order.
# Unlike gif/png's `"<name>" "{" ... "}"` collection wrapper, gltf's OWN 14 collection fields print
# through the SAME uniform `name=value` convention every scalar field uses (`enc_collection`'s
# return value is placed directly after `<name>=`, no extra wrapping braces) -- confirmed by direct
# read of `print_gltf_diff`, not assumed from another artifact's shape. Every string/byte payload is
# `hex`-encoded (`enc_str`/`enc_bytes` -> `hex_encode`) -- the framework's built-in `hex` MACRO
# (bare `hex` ident, no matching production; `Symbol::Ref`'s production-then-macro fallback,
# `match_macro_span` backtracks correctly unlike a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*` Star, §3 pitfall #2).
# `{...}*` grouping only, never bare `(...)*` (§3 pitfall #1). Kept on ONE physical line per
# production throughout (§3 pitfall #4 -- this dialect's sequence parsing stops at the first
# Newline token, no line-continuation syntax).
diff = asset-clause? scene-clause? scenes-clause? nodes-clause? meshes-clause? accessors-clause? buffer-views-clause? buffers-clause? buffer-bytes-clause? materials-clause? textures-clause? images-clause? samplers-clause? skins-clause? animations-clause? cameras-clause? extensions-used-clause? extensions-required-clause? extensions-clause? extras-clause? source-form-clause?

#region Primitives
# `Option<T>`/`Option<Option<T>>` -- `encode_option`'s uniform `[0]`/`[1,<value>]` tag; the
# tri-state form (`encode_option_option`) wraps that SAME shape one layer deeper, matching
# `png`'s/`gif`'s own `[0]`/`[1,[...]]` precedent (§1.4's tri-state pattern).

gltf-f64 = INT | FLOAT
bit-opt = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," bit "]"
f64-opt = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," gltf-f64 "]"

tri-int = "[" "0" "]" | "[" "1" "," int-opt "]"

#region GltfJsonValue
# `GltfJson` -- this artifact's own local `extras`/`extensions` value enum (F4). Tag prefix (NO

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.ply.diff
start diff

# 🎫️26/08/10/ARTIFACT-SYSTEM-OVERHAUL-REAL-CODECS-RUNTIME-REUSE-EVOLUTION FG3: real one-line
# `print_diff`/`parse_diff` form this artifact's hand-rolled `DiffCodec` (../🦀️.rs
# `print_ply_diff`/`parse_ply_diff`) emits — space-separated `name=value` token per changed
# top-level field (absent token = unchanged): `format`, `comments` (whole-vec REPLACE, NOT
# tri-state — token PRESENCE itself is the `Option` tag, there is no separate `[0]`/`[1,...]`
# wrapper around it, unlike gif89a's own tri-state fields), `elements` (the real NAME-keyed
# removed/modified triple + INDEX-keyed added triple — `PlyElementsDiff`'s own actual shape, see
# this artifact's `f6-ply-report.md` for why `elements` deliberately deviates from a uniform
# index-keyed triple). Kept on ONE physical line, matching this dialect's own sequence-parsing
# limit (no line-continuation syntax exists).
comment none

diff = format-clause? comments-clause? elements-clause?

format-clause = "format" "=" format-tag
format-tag = "a" | "l" | "b"

comments-clause = "comments" "=" "[" comment-list? "]"
comment-list = hex {"," hex}*

elements-clause = "elements" "=" elements-triple
elements-triple = "{" "[" elements-removed-list? "]" ";" "[" elements-modified-list? "]" ";" "[" elements-added-list? "]" "}"
elements-removed-list = hex {"," hex}*
elements-modified-list = elements-modified {"," elements-modified}*
elements-modified = hex ":" element-diff-value
elements-added-list = elements-added {"," elements-added}*
elements-added = INT ":" element-value

# `PlyElementDiff`'s own sparse fields print as single-letter `tag:value` pairs (`P`/`R`) inside
# its own `[...]` — `enc_element_diff`/`dec_element_diff`.
element-diff-value = "[" element-diff-items? "]"
element-diff-items = element-diff-item {"," element-diff-item}*
element-diff-item = "C" ":" INT | "P" ":" "[" property-list? "]" | "R" ":" rows-triple

rows-triple = "{" "[" rows-removed-list? "]" ";" "[" rows-modified-list? "]" ";" "[" rows-added-list? "]" "}"
rows-removed-list = INT {"," INT}*
rows-modified-list = rows-modified {"," rows-modified}*
rows-modified = INT ":" row-diff-value
rows-added-list = rows-added {"," rows-added}*
rows-added = INT ":" row-value

# `PlyRowDiff` — a bracketed list of `[name,value]` pairs — `enc_row_diff`/`dec_row_diff`.
row-diff-value = "[" row-diff-items? "]"
row-diff-items = row-diff-item {"," row-diff-item}*
row-diff-item = "[" hex "," ply-value "]"

# `PlyProperty` (data-carrying enum) — `S[name,kind]` (Scalar) / `L[name,count_kind,value_kind]`
# (List) — `enc_property`/`dec_property`.
property-list = ply-property {"," ply-property}*
ply-property = "S" "[" hex "," scalar-kind "]" | "L" "[" hex "," scalar-kind "," scalar-kind "]"
scalar-kind = "c" | "C" | "s" | "w" | "i" | "u" | "f" | "d"

# `PlyValue` (the OTHER data-carrying enum) — one lowercase tag letter (matching `scalar-kind`'s
# own letters) plus `L[...]` for the recursive `List(Vec<PlyValue>)` variant — `enc_value`/
# `dec_value`. `number` covers BOTH plain digit runs (the 6 integer kinds, and any Float/Double
# value that happens to be a whole number — Rust's own `f32`/`f64` `Display` omits the trailing
# `.0`, confirmed by this artifact's `f6-ply-report.md` worked example `value=f[42]`) and real
# decimal literals (a genuinely fractional Float/Double).
number = INT | FLOAT
ply-value = "c" "[" INT "]" | "C" "[" INT "]" | "s" "[" INT "]" | "w" "[" INT "]" | "i" "[" INT "]" | "u" "[" INT "]" | "f" "[" number "]" | "d" "[" number "]" | "L" "[" value-list? "]"
value-list = ply-value {"," ply-value}*

row-value = "[" value-list? "]"

# `PlyElement` — positional `[name,count,[properties],[rows]]` tuple — `enc_element`/`dec_element`.
element-value = "[" hex "," INT "," "[" property-list? "]" "," "[" row-list? "]" "]"
row-list = row-value {"," row-value}*

# `hex` (bare `hex`, deliberately NOT defined as a production) is the framework's built-in `hex`
# MACRO — see `📖️grammar-recipe.md` §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall #2 for why a hand-rolled `{INT|IDENT}*`
# production is wrong here (a `<digits>e<digits>` hex run can lex as one FLOAT token, silently
# desyncing a hand-rolled Star).

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.ply.mutations
start op

# 🎫️26/08/10/ARTIFACT-SYSTEM-OVERHAUL-REAL-CODECS-RUNTIME-REUSE-EVOLUTION FG3: real one-line
# `print_op`/`parse_op` form this artifact's hand-rolled `OpText` (../🦀️.rs
# `print_ply_mutation`/`parse_ply_mutation`) emits — kebab-case keyword + space-separated
# kebab-case `arg=value` tokens, one match arm per `PlyMutation` variant (no `DslVariants`
# scaffolding — nothing here derives it, `#[derive(dsl::DslOps)]` is confirmed rejected, see the
# module doc comment's real `cargo check` citation). This REPLACES the pre-Phase-2 placeholder
# this file used to contain, which described a `serde_json::to_string`-shaped JSON object line —
# stale since F6 already replaced the real `OpText`/`OpBinary` impls with this hand-rolled
# grammar; the placeholder never matched what `print_op` actually emits.
#
# Reuses the sibling `../../🔺️diff/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio`'s own `ply-value`/
# `ply-property`/`element-value`/`row-value`/`format-tag` shapes verbatim (this artifact's own
# hand-rolled Rust codec reuses `PlyDiff`'s grammar primitives the identical way — see
# `../🦀️.rs`'s own module doc comment) — RESTATED here rather than referenced, per the
# recipe's own "cross-artifact/cross-facet `use` doesn't resolve at walk time yet" rule (§2.1;
# same honest-restatement precedent zip's OPC family and svg's own xml-derived grammar establish).

set-snapshot-op = "set-snapshot" "snapshot" "=" snapshot-value
set-format-op = "set-format" "format" "=" format-tag
insert-comment-op = "insert-comment" "index" "=" INT "comment" "=" hex
remove-comment-op = "remove-comment" "index" "=" INT

remove-element-op = "remove-element" "name" "=" hex

remove-row-op = "remove-row" "element-name" "=" hex "index" "=" INT
set-row-property-op = "set-row-property" "element-name" "=" hex "row-index" "=" INT "property-name" "=" hex "value" "=" ply-value

format-tag = "a" | "l" | "b"

# `PlySnapshot` — positional `[schema,format,[comments],[elements]]` tuple — `enc_snapshot`/
# `dec_snapshot` (../🦀️.rs).

property-list = ply-property {"," ply-property}*
ply-property = "S" "[" hex "," scalar-kind "]" | "L" "[" hex "," scalar-kind "," scalar-kind "]"
scalar-kind = "c" | "C" | "s" | "w" | "i" | "u" | "f" | "d"

row-list = row-value {"," row-value}*
row-value = "[" value-list? "]"
value-list = ply-value {"," ply-value}*

number = INT | FLOAT
ply-value = "c" "[" INT "]" | "C" "[" INT "]" | "s" "[" INT "]" | "w" "[" INT "]" | "i" "[" INT "]" | "u" "[" INT "]" | "f" "[" number "]" | "d" "[" number "]" | "L" "[" value-list? "]"

# `hex` (bare `hex`, deliberately NOT defined as a production) is the framework's built-in `hex`

dialect grammar
grammar json.diff
extension json
start document

# P2-P1: real one-line `DiffCodec::print_diff`/`parse_diff` shape ALREADY emitted by
# `🧾️json/…/🔺️diff/🦀️.rs` (`print_json_diff`/`parse_json_diff`) — replaces the F6-era
# placeholder describing a serde-JSON `JsonDiff` wire struct the codec never emits. `JsonDiff` has
# exactly one diffable field (`schema` is identity-only, never diffed — see that file's own doc
# comment), so the line is either EMPTY (unchanged: `d.value == None`) or exactly one
# `value=<value-diff>` token — `document`'s `?` makes the whole line optional, correctly recognizing
# the empty string (`Optional` degrades to a no-op when its inner `Ref` fails to match at an empty
# token stream, same mechanism used by the `?` on every list item below).
document = value-line?
value-line = "value" "=" value-diff

# `enc_value_diff` / `dec_value_diff` — `JsonValueDiff` needs its own tag (`R`=Replace in addition
# to `B`/`N`/`S`/`A`/`O`) since, unlike a bare `JsonValue`, it can appear standalone at the top-level
# `value=` token position, not only nested inside a bracketed container. Genuinely recursive: `A`/`O`
# reference `value-diff` (via `array-modified-item`/`object-modified-item`) which references them
# back through nested collection diffs — exercised end-to-end by this artifact's own
# `diff_grammar_conformance_law` test against real `print_diff` output covering every
# `JsonValueDiff` variant, incl. the `Replace` kind-change fallback and nested array/object triples.
value-diff = "R" "[" value "]" | "B" "[" INT "]" | "N" "[" hex "]" | "S" "[" hex "]" | "A" "[" array-diff-body "]" | "O" "[" object-diff-body "]"

# `enc_array_diff`/`dec_array_diff` — `[removed];[modified];[added]`, index-keyed.
array-diff-body = "[" array-removed-item* "]" ";" "[" array-modified-item* "]" ";" "[" array-added-item* "]"
array-removed-item = INT ","?
array-modified-item = INT ":" value-diff ","?
array-added-item = INT ":" value ","?

# `enc_object_diff`/`dec_object_diff` — `[removed];[modified];[added]`, name-keyed (`added` entries
# additionally carry the FINAL Vec position ahead of the hex-encoded key: `index:key:item`).
object-diff-body = "[" object-removed-item* "]" ";" "[" object-modified-item* "]" ";" "[" object-added-item* "]"
object-removed-item = hex ","?
object-modified-item = hex ":" value-diff ","?
object-added-item = INT ":" hex ":" value ","?

# `enc_json_value`/`dec_json_value` — restated here (same shape as the sibling
# ../../📸️snapshot/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio's `value`/../../🧬️mutations/📝️text's `value`)
# so this leaf grammar is self-contained, matching the repo's existing per-facet convention.
value = "Z" | "B" "[" INT "]" | "N" "[" hex "]" | "S" "[" hex "]" | "A" "[" arr-item* "]" | "O" "[" obj-item* "]"
arr-item = value ","?
obj-item = hex ":" value ","?

# `hex` (bare `hex`, deliberately NOT defined as a production here) is the framework's built-in `hex`
# MACRO (`📖️grammar/🦀️.rs`'s `default_macros`/`macro_hex_ok`), not a
# `hex = {INT | IDENT}*`-shaped production — see the sibling
# `../../🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio`'s `hex` doc comment for why: a production's
# `Star` never backtracks, and (separately) a `<digits>e<digits>` hex run lexes as one `FLOAT` token,
# not alternating `INT`/`IDENT`; the macro's own backtracking (`Recognizer::match_macro_span`)
# handles both, with no grammar-file workaround needed.

# ARTIFACT-SYSTEM-OVERHAUL-REAL-CODECS-RUNTIME-REUSE-EVOLUTION brep wave (following the flow
# pilot's proven template, `ws-codec-workflow-report.md`). Real grammar for
# `SemioBrepSnapshot::print_dsl`/`parse_dsl` (📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs's `print_brep_snapshot_body`/
# `parse_brep_snapshot_body`) — hand-rolled (curve/surface are data-carrying tagged enums; a
# derive-path `RecordSpec` cannot express the `L[...]`/`C[...]`/`N[...]`-tagged text shape). Same
# hex/bracket-encoded value convention as this subset's own `🔺️diff`/`🧬️mutations` facet grammars.
#
# `document` matches the fixture-honesty harness's own reconstructed body shape (mandatory `semio
# stdio.semio.brep.dsl v1` preamble stripped and replaced with the bare `envelope_id()` token —
# `artifact-mark` below — before recognition, same convention `json.snapshot`'s own grammar uses).
artifact-mark = "stdio.semio.brep"
document = artifact-mark schema-line vertices-line edges-line loops-line faces-line shells-line solids-line coedges-line next-label-line

schema-line = "schema" "=" hex

vertices-line = "vertices" "=" "[" vertex-items? "]"
vertex-items = vertex {"," vertex}*
edges-line = "edges" "=" "[" edge-items? "]"
edge-items = edge {"," edge}*
loops-line = "loops" "=" "[" brep-loop-items? "]"
brep-loop-items = brep-loop {"," brep-loop}*
faces-line = "faces" "=" "[" face-items? "]"
face-items = face {"," face}*
shells-line = "shells" "=" "[" shell-items? "]"
shell-items = shell {"," shell}*
solids-line = "solids" "=" "[" solid-items? "]"
solid-items = solid {"," solid}*
# 🧱️ Landed alongside `BrepCoedge`/`SemioBrepSnapshot::next_label`
# (ticket 26/09/03/BREP-KERNEL-DEPENDENCY-FREE-RUNTIME wave W3-A) — the p-curve/ring/label-
# high-water-mark fields the native `Body` carries that the pre-wave snapshot dropped (see
# `📸️snapshot/🔁️body/🦀️.rs`'s module doc for the full round-trip rationale).
coedges-line = "coedges" "=" "[" coedge-items? "]"
coedge-items = coedge {"," coedge}*
next-label-line = "nextLabel" "=" number

# Entity value grammars — field order matches `enc_vertex`/`enc_edge`/`enc_loop`/`enc_face`/
# `enc_shell`/`enc_solid`/`enc_coedge` in `📸️snapshot/🦀️.rs` exactly (the authoritative source).
vertex = "[" hex "," point3 "," number "]"
edge = "[" hex "," hex "," hex "," curve "," number "]"
brep-loop = "[" hex "," loop-edge-list "]"
face = "[" hex "," hex "," hex-list "," surface "," bool "," number "]"
shell = "[" hex "," shell-face-list "]"
solid = "[" hex "," solid-shell-list "]"

# `BrepCoedge`: `[id,edge,forward,pcurve,prange,loopId,next,prev]`, field order matching
# `enc_coedge` exactly. `pcurve` is `-` for `None` or `~` followed by a tagged `curve2` for
# `Some` (`enc_opt_curve2`); `prange` is a plain `[start,end]` number pair (`enc_prange`).
coedge = "[" hex "," hex "," bool "," opt-curve2 "," prange "," hex "," hex "," hex "]"
opt-curve2 = "-" | "~" curve2
prange = "[" number "," number "]"

# `BrepCurve2` (the p-curve type — same tag/bracket convention as `curve` below, one dimension
# down): `L[origin,direction]` (Line) / `C[center,radius]` (Circle) /
# `E[center,xAxis,radiusMajor,radiusMinor]` (Ellipse) / `N[controlPoints,weights,degree,knots]`
# (Nurbs).
curve2 = "L" "[" point2 "," point2 "]" | "C" "[" point2 "," number "]" | "E" "[" point2 "," point2 "," number "," number "]" | "N" "[" point2-list "," number-list "," number "," number-list "]"
point2 = "[" number "," number "]"
point2-list = "[" point2-items? "]"
point2-items = point2 {"," point2}*

loop-edge = "[" hex "," bool "]"
loop-edge-list = "[" loop-edge-items? "]"
loop-edge-items = loop-edge {"," loop-edge}*
shell-face = "[" hex "," bool "]"
shell-face-list = "[" shell-face-items? "]"
shell-face-items = shell-face {"," shell-face}*
solid-shell = "[" hex "," bool "]"
solid-shell-list = "[" solid-shell-items? "]"
solid-shell-items = solid-shell {"," solid-shell}*
hex-list = "[" hex-items? "]"
hex-items = loop-id {"," loop-id}*
loop-id = "[" hex "]"

# `BrepCurve`: `L[origin,direction]` (Line) / `C[center,axis,radius]` (Circle) /
# `E[center,axis,radiusMajor,radiusMinor]` (Ellipse) / `N[controlPoints,weights,degree,knots]`
# (Nurbs) — single-letter tag prefix, same convention `enc_curve` (🔺️diff/🦀️.rs, the
# established precedent this facet's own encoder matches field-for-field) uses.
curve = "L" "[" point3 "," point3 "]" | "C" "[" point3 "," point3 "," number "]" | "E" "[" point3 "," point3 "," number "," number "]" | "N" "[" point3-list "," number-list "," number "," number-list "]"

# `BrepSurface`: `P[origin,normal]` (Plane) / `C[origin,axis,radius]` (Cylinder) /
# `O[origin,axis,radius,halfAngle]` (Cone) / `S[center,radius]` (Sphere) /
# `T[center,axis,majorRadius,minorRadius]` (Torus) /
# `N[controlPoints,weights,uCount,vCount,degreeU,degreeV,knotsU,knotsV]` (Nurbs).
surface = "P" "[" point3 "," point3 "]" | "C" "[" point3 "," point3 "," number "]" | "O" "[" point3 "," point3 "," number "," number "]" | "S" "[" point3 "," number "]" | "T" "[" point3 "," point3 "," number "," number "]" | "N" "[" point3-list "," number-list "," number "," number "," number "," number "," number-list "," number-list "]"

point3 = "[" number "," number "," number "]"
point3-list = "[" point3-items? "]"
point3-items = point3 {"," point3}*
number-list = "[" number-items? "]"
number-items = number {"," number}*
bool = "0" | "1"

# `SemioPoint3.x`/`.y`/`.z` and every `f64`/`u32` field print via plain Rust `{v}` Display — the
# shared lexer's `INT`/`FLOAT` scanners already capture a leading `-` when digit-adjacent (P2-M1's
# trailing-dot-float work), matching `enc_f64` lexeme-for-lexeme.
number = INT | FLOAT | IDENT | "-" "inf"

# `hex` (bare `hex`, deliberately NOT defined as a production here) is the framework's built-in
# `hex` MACRO (`📖️grammar/🦀️.rs`'s `default_macros`) — every `id`/`schema` leaf string is

# P2-FG2: real M1 grammar dialect, replacing the pre-M1 ABNF-styled placeholder this file used
# to hold. BMP has no textual syntax of its own -- `store::ArtifactDsl::print_dsl`/`parse_dsl`
# (../../🦀️.rs, the `HandcraftedArtifactCodecs` region) hex-encode/decode the REAL
# on-disk BMP file bytes (BITMAPFILEHEADER + BITMAPINFOHEADER + optional masks/palette + pixel
# data) verbatim, byte-for-byte -- this is bmp's own honest precedent from Phase 1's survey
# (P2-W0 §1b), mirrored here on png's own already-real snapshot/text grammar
# (`🔣️png/…/📸️snapshot/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio`), not aspirational. See
# ../💾️binary/📡️.protocol.semio for that same binary's real structural grammar
# (field-by-field BITMAPFILEHEADER/BITMAPINFOHEADER/masks/palette/pixel-data).
comment none

# `dsl::fixture_sweep`'s `dsl_body_from_fixture` feeds the Recognizer "<envelope-id>\n<body>"
# (`SemioEnvelope::envelope_id` = "stdio.bmp", the real preamble line's own trailing "v<n>"
# already stripped by the harness) -- the shared lexer treats the preamble's newline as trivia,
# so `envelope-mark` and the hex body sit directly adjacent in the significant token stream,
# matching json/csv/png's own grammars' identical convention.
envelope-mark = "stdio.bmp"
document = envelope-mark hex-body

# The rest of the DSL text is one lowercase-hex digit run -- the real BMP file's bytes, hex-
# encoded losslessly (`engine::encode_bmp`/`decode_bmp`, ../../⚙️engine/🦀️.rs).
# `hex` (bare `hex`, deliberately NOT defined as a production here) is the framework's built-in
# `hex` MACRO (`📖️grammar/🦀️.rs`'s `default_macros`/`macro_hex_ok`) -- the dialect
# recipe's own documented rule (this ticket's own recipe §1.3(f)/§3 pitfall #2): a hand-rolled
# `{INT | IDENT}*`-shaped production would silently mis-lex a `<digits>e<digits>` byte run as one
# FLOAT token instead of alternating INT/IDENT; the macro's own largest-span-first backtracking
# (`Recognizer::match_macro_span`) handles it correctly with no grammar-file workaround needed.
hex-body = hex

dialect grammar
grammar stdio.bmp.diff
start diff

# P2-FG2: real one-line `print_diff`/`parse_diff` form -- `BmpDiff` derives `dsl::DslDiff`, whose
# `DiffCodec::print_diff` is `dsl::print(&self.__dsl_diff_to_record(), &Self::__dsl_diff_spec(),
# dsl::JoinMode::Inline)` -- the SAME generic derive-driven printer the sibling mutations grammar
# (../../🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio) documents. This file used to (wrongly)
# document the wire text as a bare JSON serialization -- replaced here after tracing the real
# function, not guessed, per this ticket's own recipe §4 checklist item. `BmpDiff` has no
# container keyword (no `#[dsl(keyword = "...")]` attribute is set on it) -- every field prints
# as a bare `key=value`/`key { ... }` run, no leading tag. Every top-level field is `Option<T>`
# (present = changed, absent = unchanged); an all-`None` diff prints as the empty string. Field
# print ORDER is rank-then-declaration-order (`keyed_field_rank`, 🗣️dsl/🧬️schema/🦀️.rs):
# every scalar header field is rank 0 (declaration order); `palette` (`#[dsl(block)]`) and
# `pixels` (plain `Option<Vec<u8>>` -- the derive's `classify_field` peels the `Option` layer
# before checking `#[dsl(base64)]`, so it silently falls back to a bracketed `Vec<INT>` list
# rather than base64 -- documented quirk, ../🦀️.rs's own doc comment) are BOTH rank 1,
# so their DECLARATION order (`palette` before `pixels` in the struct) decides, which happens to
# match print order here too. Verified against a real `BmpDiff::between(a, b).print_diff()` call
# (recorded runtime probe): `"header-size=56 width=8 height=6 row-order=top-down
# planes=2 bits-per-pixel=24 compression=3 image-size=200 x-pixels-per-meter=3000
# y-pixels-per-meter=4000 colors-used=5 colors-important=2 palette { removed=[ ]
# modified=[ index=1 entry { b=99 g=88 r=77 reserved=1 } ] added=[ index=2 entry { b=200 g=201
# r=202 reserved=0 } ] } pixels=[ 3 10 17 ... ]"`.
comment none

diff = header-size-field? width-field? height-field? row-order-field? planes-field? bits-per-pixel-field? compression-field? image-size-field? x-ppm-field? y-ppm-field? colors-used-field? colors-important-field? palette-field? pixels-field?

header-size-field = "header-size" "=" INT
width-field = "width" "=" INT
height-field = "height" "=" INT
row-order-field = "row-order" "=" row-order-value
row-order-value = "bottom-up" | "top-down"
planes-field = "planes" "=" INT
bits-per-pixel-field = "bits-per-pixel" "=" INT
compression-field = "compression" "=" INT
image-size-field = "image-size" "=" INT
x-ppm-field = "x-pixels-per-meter" "=" INT
y-ppm-field = "y-pixels-per-meter" "=" INT
colors-used-field = "colors-used" "=" INT
colors-important-field = "colors-important" "=" INT

# `BmpPaletteDiff` is itself a keyword-less `#[derive(dsl::DslRecord)]` struct -- a `Block`-shaped
# field prints as a bare leading keyword (`"palette { ... }"`, never `"palette={...}"`,
# `print_record_fields`'s own `Shape::Block` arm) wrapping its own 3 keyed fields (all rank 1
# `List`s, so declaration order: `removed`, `modified`, `added`).
palette-field = "palette" "{" removed-field modified-field added-field "}"
removed-field = "removed" "=" "[" INT* "]"
modified-field = "modified" "=" "[" palette-modified-entry* "]"
added-field = "added" "=" "[" palette-added-entry* "]"

# `BmpPaletteModified`/`BmpPaletteAdded` are likewise keyword-less `#[derive(dsl::DslRecord)]`
# structs: `index` (rank 0 scalar) then `entry` (rank 1 block, `BmpPaletteEntry`'s own 4 scalar
# fields in declaration order) -- list-of-record boundary recovery is structural, the same "next
# item's own leading key IS the boundary" pattern the sibling mutations grammar's
# `insert-palette-entry`/`set-palette-entry` already rely on.
palette-modified-entry = "index" "=" INT "entry" "{" palette-entry-fields "}"
palette-added-entry = "index" "=" INT "entry" "{" palette-entry-fields "}"
palette-entry-fields = "b" "=" INT "g" "=" INT "r" "=" INT "reserved" "=" INT

# `pixels: Option<Vec<u8>>` -- no `#[dsl(block)]`/`#[dsl(base64)]` reaches through the `Option`
# layer (documented derive quirk above), so this prints as a bare bracketed `INT` list, one item
# per decoded RGBA byte, no separators (same "next real field's own leading key/bracket IS the
# boundary" structural recovery every other list in this grammar family relies on).
pixels-field = "pixels" "=" "[" INT* "]"
